lessons.title: Reading what is not said: presupposition, implication and hedging
lessons.explanation: A text communicates more than its sentences assert, and in Russian notices, advertisements and official letters the extra content is often the point. This lesson gives you the three mechanisms that produce it, and the Russian words that mark them. The first mechanism is presupposition: a sentence can only be understood if something else is already assumed. Wikipedia's article states the condition exactly: 'A presupposition of a sentence must normally be part of the common ground of the utterance context (the shared knowledge of the interlocutors) in order for the sentence to be felicitous.' Russian marks presupposition with a small set of triggers. Как известно (kak eez-VYES-na), 'as is known', asserts that you already know what follows and thereby moves it out of the area where you might ask whether it is true. Напоминаем (na-pee-mee-NA-yem), 'we remind you', presupposes that you were told before. A change-of-state verb such as перестал, 'stopped', presupposes that the earlier state existed, and it keeps that presupposition under negation: он не перестал курить does not mean 'he never smoked'. The article lists the same triggers in English: definite descriptions, factive verbs, implicative verbs, change-of-state verbs, iteratives such as опять and снова, temporal clauses, cleft sentences, comparisons and contrasts, counterfactual conditionals, questions, and possessives. The second mechanism is implicature, which is what a speaker means without saying. The classic account is Grice's, and the encyclopaedia's example is worth learning literally: 'A (to passerby): I am out of gas. B: There is a gas station 'round the corner. Here, B does not say, but conversationally implicates, that the gas station is open, because otherwise his utterance would not be relevant in the context.' That is why мол (MOL) and дескать (DYES-kat), the colloquial quotative particles meaning roughly 'says he' and 'supposedly', are so useful to a reader: they mark a claim as someone else's words while refusing to vouch for it. To name the mechanism itself, Russian has подразумевать (pad-ra-zoo-mee-VAT), 'to imply, to mean implicitly', and its noun намёк (na-MYOK), 'a hint'. Related items are якобы (YA-by), 'allegedly' — which signals that the writer does not assert the claim and is usually a warning that you should not either — and будто (BOOD-ta), 'as if, that (doubtfully)', used both for reported speech the writer distrusts and for comparisons. The third mechanism is hedging, and its function is to reduce commitment without removing the claim. Wikipedia notes that 'Linguists consider hedges to be tools of epistemic modality; allowing speakers and writers to signal a level of caution in making an assertion.' In official Russian the workhorses are возможны (vaz-MOZH-ny), 'possible, may be', which promises nothing, от plus a figure (от шестидесяти тысяч), which gives a floor rather than a rate, тем не менее (tyem nye MYE-nye-ye), 'nevertheless', which concedes and continues, and само собой (sa-MO sa-BOY), 'of course, it stands to reason', which invites agreement rather than offering evidence. Finally, negation has scope. Cornell's grammar makes the contrast that matters: unstressed ни in никуда, никогда, никто goes with a negated verb, while stressed не in некуда, некогда, нечего is a predicative meaning 'there is no ...' — as in негде (NYE-gdye) жить, 'there is nowhere to live', where the preposition splits the prefix from the question word. Reading a negation therefore means asking not only what is denied but what is denied to whom, and whether the денотат (dye-na-TAT), the thing talked about, is presupposed to exist at all.
lessons.example: Here is an authored notice of the kind that appears on the door of a Russian apartment block; the text is written for this lesson, not copied from a real notice. Уважаемые жильцы! В связи с плановым ремонтом горячей воды не будет с 12 по 20 июля. Как известно, такие работы проводятся ежегодно. Напоминаем, что заявки на перерасчёт принимаются только при наличии акта. Очевидно, что сроки могут быть продлены. Не случайно мы рекомендуем заранее проверить счётчики. (oo-va-ZHA-ye-my ZHEEL-tsy! f svya-ZEE s PLA-na-vym ree-MON-tam ga-RYA-chey va-DY nye BOO-deet s dvee-NAT-tsa-ta-va pa dva-TSAT-tsa-ta-va ee-YU-lya. kak eez-VYES-na, ta-KEE-ye ra-BO-ty pra-VO-dyat-sya ye-zhe-GOD-na. na-pee-mee-NA-yem, shto za-YAF-kee na pee-ree-ra-SHCHOT pree-nee-MA-yut-sya TOL-ka pree na-LEE-chee ee AK-ta. a-chee-VEED-na, shto SRYER-kee MO-goot byt prad-LYEN-ny. nye sloo-CHAY-na my ree-ka-men-DOO-yem za-RA-ne-ye pra-VYE-reet SHCHOT-chee-kee.) The notice asserts five things and presupposes eight. Asserted: there is no hot water from 12 to 20 July; the work is annual; claims for recalculation are accepted only with a certificate; the deadline may be extended; the reader is advised to check the meters in advance. Presupposed but never stated: that a schedule of works exists and is planned, since плановым treats it as given; that such work happens every year, which как известно presents as common ground and so removes the question 'is this true of this building?'; that a previous notification was given, which напоминаем introduces; that repair work will in fact have happened, which the reader must accept in order to want a recalculation at all; that some residents will lack the certificate, which only при наличии акта implies; that the extension is a real possibility rather than a formality, which очевидно dresses as an inference the writer shares with you; and that there is a reason for the recommendation, which не случайно insinuates without naming. Now the implications. Могут быть продлены is a hedge: it says the deadline may be extended, and in the context of a service notice it invites the reader to plan for the extension without obliging anyone to announce one. Только при наличии акта is a stronger restriction than its grammar suggests, because the acceptance of claims is conditional on a document the notice never tells you how to obtain. And the negation in горячей воды не будет keeps the presupposition of planned work: negating the water supply does not negate the repair. A reader who writes down 'the notice promised hot water back on 20 July' has read the assertion and lost two of the presuppositions and both hedges.
lessons.question: Which sentence of the notice does the most work by pretending that something is already known, and what does a careful reader do with it?
lessons.answer: Как известно, такие работы проводятся ежегодно — 'as is known, such work is carried out every year' — because как известно presupposes that the reader already shares the information, so the reader should treat the annual schedule as a claim to be checked against previous years rather than as a fact the writer has established.
lessons.distractor: Очевидно, что сроки могут быть продлены — because очевидно is the strongest marker of shared knowledge and the extension is the notice's real content.
lessons.correction: Очевидно does not claim shared knowledge; it claims that a conclusion follows from something already present, and in this notice it introduces the writer's own inference about the deadline. Как известно is the genuine presupposition trigger: it moves its content into the common ground and thereby removes the natural question 'is this true here?'. The practical move for a reader is to ask what would be different if the phrase were removed: with как известно the annual schedule looks like background; without it, the same sentence becomes a naked claim that someone must be able to support. That test — delete the trigger and see what has to be proved — is the whole diagnostic for presupposition.

depth.definitions: Presupposition is content a sentence takes for granted rather than asserts; a presupposition trigger is a word or construction that produces it (definite descriptions, factive and implicative verbs, change-of-state verbs, iteratives, temporal clauses, clefts, comparisons, counterfactual conditionals, questions, possessives). Implicature is what a speaker means without saying it, arising from the expectation that utterances are relevant and cooperative; it is cancellable, which a logical consequence is not. A hedge is a device that lowers the speaker's commitment: possible, allegedly, on average, up to, from (a figure). A quotative particle is a word such as мол or дескать that marks words as someone else's. Evidentiality is the marking of how a speaker knows. Scope of negation is the stretch of a sentence a negative element affects. Prerequisites: the uncertainty and evidentiality material of lesson 86, the impersonal and passive constructions of lesson 83, the close-reading method of lesson 81, the reported speech of lesson 76, and the genitive for absence of lessons 53-54, because негде and its relatives behave like the нет-construction.
depth.mechanism: Why do texts presuppose instead of asserting? Because a presupposition cannot easily be denied, and because it moves content into a region where the reader's attention is low. The mechanism is visible in the notice: напоминаем turns the writer's content into a reminder about your own prior knowledge, and как известно does the same for an annual schedule the writer may not have verified for this building. Grice's account of implicature explains the other half: an utterance is interpreted against the assumption that it is relevant, so a sentence that merely describes a nearby petrol station is understood as saying that it is open, because the description would be pointless otherwise. Note the limit that Wikipedia states: implicatures 'are not necessary or logical consequences of what is said, but are defeasible (cancellable)' — the speaker can withdraw the implication without contradicting themselves, which is exactly why a contract, a notice or an advertisement can rely on them while denying them. Presupposition has a related limit. The article records that a presupposition which is not in the common ground is normally 'accommodated': the reader silently adds it to make the sentence work. Accommodation is the reader's own contribution, and it is the moment at which a text can smuggle in a false premise: you have to assume that something is common knowledge in order to understand the sentence, and the assumption then feels like your own discovery. The defence is procedural rather than grammatical: for every presupposition trigger you meet, write down what it requires you to accept, and check that item separately.
depth.secondExample: Here is a second authored text, a job advertisement with the same machinery under commercial pressure. Молодой, динамично развивающейся компании требуется специалист по логистике. Заработная плата — от шестидесяти тысяч рублей. Возможны командировки. Мы ищем человека, который не боится ответственности и умеет работать в условиях неопределённости. Опыт от года будет преимуществом. (ma-la-DOY, dee-na-MEECH-na raz-vee-VA-yoo-shchey-sya kam-PA-nee-ee TRE-boo-yet-sya spye-tsee-a-LEEST pa la-GEES-tee-kye. ZA-ra-bat-na-ya PLA-ta — at shees-tee-dee-SYA-tee TY-seech ROOB-lyey. vaz-MOZH-ny ka-man-dee-ROF-kee. my EE-shchem chee-la-VYE-ka, ka-TO-ry nye ba-EET-sya at-VYET-stvyen-nas-tee ee oo-MYE-yet ra-BO-tat f oos-LO-vee-yakh nee-ap-ree-dye-LYON-nas-tee. O-pyt at GO-da BOO-deet pree-ee-MOO-shche-stvam.) Read what is not written. От шестидесяти тысяч is a floor, not a salary: the addressee knows the official number and the applicant does not, and the formula is legal while being uninformative, which is precisely the point of a hedge. Возможны командировки implicates that travel may be required without promising compensation or frequency; the word возможны is doing the work that a contract would have to do differently. Не боится ответственности and в условиях неопределённости together implicate that the role carries unresolved pressure and that the previous holder found it hard — an inference the advertisement never states and could deny, which is exactly the cancellation property of implicature. Опыт от года будет преимуществом is a classic double hedge: the requirement is one year, and even that is only an advantage, so nothing in the text excludes a candidate with no experience and nothing promises that experience will help. There are presuppositions too: требуется специалист presupposes that the position exists and is funded; динамично развивающейся presupposes change, which in a job advertisement usually implies instability; ищем человека ... который presupposes a defined type of person and thereby classifies the reader before reading the letter. The reading skill is not cynicism. It is the discipline of writing, beside each sentence, what it asserts, what it presupposes and what it invites you to infer, and then deciding which of the three you are prepared to rely on.
depth.mistake: The characteristic error is to treat hedges and presupposition triggers as empty style. Four specific traps. (1) Как известно is read as evidence, so the content that follows is filed as established; the correct move is to treat it as a claim wearing the clothes of shared knowledge. (2) Якобы and мол/дескать are read as ordinary quotation, so the reader adopts the reported content; in fact якобы marks the writer's refusal to vouch for a claim, and a very common Russian news-reading error is to attribute the speaker's claim to the newspaper because the newspaper merely reported that someone said it. (3) Возможны and от (plus a figure) are read as promises, which turns an advertisement into a contract that does not exist. (4) Prefixed negation is read as one meaning: негде, некогда, нечего mean 'there is no place, no time, nothing', while нигде, никогда, ничего mean 'nowhere, never, nothing at all' inside a negated clause, and the two cannot be substituted without changing what the sentence claims to exist. Diagnostic procedure: for a paragraph, draw three columns and write each sentence's assertion, its presuppositions and its invitations separately. Then ask, sentence by sentence, 'if this column were false, would the text still work?' A presupposition that fails makes the sentence unusable; an implicature that fails only makes the writer misleading. That difference is what you need in order to decide how much to rely on a document.
depth.application: Nonblocking task. Take one real Russian text of the kind that makes demands on you — an apartment notice, an insurance summary, a course description, a job advertisement, a rental listing — and produce a three-column table of assertions, presuppositions and invitations for at least five sentences, quoting the trigger for each row. Then write two short texts of your own: first, a hundred-word English summary that keeps only the assertions; second, one paragraph listing every question you would have to ask the writer before relying on the document. Model response for the job advertisement: assertions — the company is hiring a logistics specialist, the advertised pay starts at 60,000 roubles, business travel is possible, experience of one year is an advantage. Presuppositions — a position exists and is funded; the company is changing; a particular kind of person is being sought. Invitations — travel will be required; the role is stressful; the previous holder struggled; applicants without experience are not excluded. Questions to ask: what are the working hours and the full salary range; how frequent is the travel and who pays; what does 'working under uncertainty' mean in this role week to week; is the one-year experience a preference or a filter; who decides. Self-review rubric, five points: (1) every row quotes the Russian trigger that produced it; (2) no inference has been placed in the assertion column; (3) at least one row is marked 'accommodated by me, not licensed by the text'; (4) your questions are answerable by a person, not rhetorical; (5) you did not convert any hedge into a promise in your summary. This is a comprehension exercise. It does not constitute legal, medical or financial advice, and for a document that obliges you to something, the questions in your second list belong to a qualified human reader, not to a language course.
depth.summary: Meaning in a Russian official text is distributed across three layers: what is asserted, what is presupposed, and what is invited. Прескрипции of the language mark the layers — как известно and напоминаем for presupposition, мол, дескать, якобы and будто for attributed or doubted speech, возможны, от plus a figure, тем не менее and само собой for reduced commitment, and the не-/ни- pair for the scope of negation. Because presuppositions must be accommodated and implicatures can be cancelled, a text can commit its reader to more than it has claimed, and the defence is a written three-column analysis rather than suspicion. This closes the reading unit. In the second unit you will produce texts of your own, and you will then be on the other side of the same mechanism: the summary, the request, the argument and the recommendation you write will all be read by someone applying exactly these tests, which is why the next lesson begins with the discipline of saying only what you can support.

visual.title: Three-column extraction of unstated meaning
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: a table with one row per sentence and three fixed columns — asserted, presupposed, invited — plus a trigger column, applied to the notice and the job advertisement. Rendered as text steps, not as video or animation.
steps: Step 1 — Sentence inventory. Number the sentences and copy the main clause of each into column one without adding anything. Output: a list of pure assertions, no adjectives you supplied.

Step 2 — Trigger hunt. Circle every presupposition trigger (как известно, напоминаем, только при наличии, перестал, опять, снова) and write in column two what each one requires the reader to accept. Output: a presupposition list in which every row names its trigger.

Step 3 — Invitation list. In column three write what the text invites you to conclude but does not claim (may be extended, travel will be required, the role is stressful), and mark each row 'cancellable'. Output: an inference list separated from the first two columns.
Step 4 — Accommodation audit. Mark any presupposition you supplied yourself rather than receiving from the text, and state where you got it. Output: at least one row labelled 'accommodated by me'.

Step 5 — Reliance decision. For each row write one of three verdicts: rely on it, ask the writer about it, or ignore it — with a one-line reason. Output: a table you could take to a conversation, not a verdict about any document's legality.

questions.prompt: A short report runs: «По данным Минтранса, ремонт дороги завершат до конца года. Как сообщает издание «Дорожные вести» со ссылкой на источник в министерстве, финансирование уже согласовано.» Which sentence can the reader trace to an accountable source, which cannot, and what does the difference change for a reader who has to act on it?
questions.answer: The first is traceable: it names Минтранс and hands the claim to a document through по данным, so the document can be requested and the institution can be asked. The second is not: it reports only that a publication cites an unnamed source inside the ministry, so nobody identifiable stands behind the funding claim. The difference changes whether the reader can contest the claim before acting, not whether it is true.
questions.distractor: Both sentences are equally traceable, because each one names the ministry; по данным and со ссылкой на are two spellings of the same attribution.
questions.correction: по данным names a document as the basis of a claim, while со ссылкой на followed by источник в министерстве names only that a claim was heard somewhere. Attribution tracks accountability, not topic: two sentences can both mention a ministry and differ completely in who can be asked to defend them. The reading routine is to follow the chain one link back and mark it traceable or unreachable; only the first sentence survives that test, and a reader who must decide something today should say so in writing rather than treat the two as equivalents.

questions.prompt: A notice on a laboratory door reads: «Посетителям не разрешается входить в лабораторию без сопровождения. Не надо оставлять сумки в коридоре. При необходимости обратитесь к дежурному.» What does each obligation bind, and how should the second sentence be read?
questions.answer: The first binds посетителям in the dative and states a prohibition with a reflexive passive; the second uses не надо, whose usual reading is a prohibition rather than 'you need not', so a careful reader treats it as a rule and looks for можно не if the text meant the action was optional. The third names no obligee at all and refers to дежурному in the dative as the person spoken to.
questions.distractor: The second sentence means there is no obligation, so leaving bags in the corridor is permitted; не надо always marks a missing requirement.
questions.correction: не надо is ambiguous between 'must not' and 'need not', and the usual interpretation is the prohibition, which Cornell's grammar states directly; the unambiguous way to say 'you don't have to' is a form of мочь with не before an imperfective infinitive, as in можно не оставлять. In a rule text the practical asymmetry decides the reading: adopting the permissive interpretation when the writer meant a prohibition breaks a rule, while adopting the prohibitive reading when the writer meant a choice costs only a question. Note also that the dative in посетителям and in обратитесь к дежурному marks two different roles — the person bound and the person to ask — and the register leaves both unnamed as individuals.

questions.prompt: In one personal passage a narrator writes «Я давно занимаюсь русским» and two sentences later «Об этих курсах я узнала давно». A reader renders both with 'long ago' and finds the next sentence — about what she still cannot do — contradictory. What has the reader done wrong?
questions.answer: The rendering has erased a tense distinction: with a non-past imperfective verb давно means 'for a long time now', so я давно занимаюсь describes a habit still running, while with a past verb давно means 'long ago', so я узнала давно describes a finished event. Keeping the two apart removes the contradiction, because the habit is still in progress when the narrator lists what she still finds hard.
questions.distractor: Nothing is wrong: давно is an adverb of past time, so both sentences refer to the past and the narrator's later difficulty shows that her first claim was inaccurate.
questions.correction: давно carries no tense of its own; the verb's tense supplies the meaning, and this is precisely why the adverb is worth slowing down for. Reading the first sentence as past turns an ongoing practice into a closed decision, which then collides with the narrator's present-tense difficulties. A second marker is doing related work in the same passage: «зато» concedes a loss and points to a compensating gain in one movement, so the following clause explains how both statements can be true at once rather than contradicting the earlier one.

questions.prompt: A regional release says: «Доля семей с детьми выросла с 12 до 18 процентов, рост составил 6 процентов.» A reader wants to quote the change in a summary. Recompute the figures and state what the sentence mixes up.
questions.answer: The rise is 6 percentage points, not 6 percent; as a relative change it is 50 percent, because 18 divided by 12 equals 1.5. The sentence has stated a difference between two rates in the unit of the rates themselves, and a reader quoting 'рост 6 процентов' would be repeating a unit error that changes the size of the change by a factor of more than eight.
questions.distractor: The sentence is correct: 18 minus 12 equals 6, and a difference of six in percentage figures is six percent.
questions.correction: A difference between two percentages is measured in percentage points, while a change in the underlying quantity is measured in percent of a base. 18 minus 12 equals 6 percentage points, and 18 divided by 12 equals 1.5, so the relative change is 50 percent. Both statements are true and neither is the other one. The safe summary names the unit and the base explicitly, and, where the text does not supply the base, records that it is missing rather than inferring it.

questions.prompt: A job advertisement reads: «Заработная плата — от шестидесяти тысяч рублей. Возможны командировки. Ищем человека, который не боится ответственности.» A reader writes to the advertiser expecting 60,000 roubles and paid travel. Which layer of meaning has the reader confused?
questions.answer: The reader has promoted invitations and hedges into assertions: от plus a figure is a floor rather than a rate, возможны marks a possibility the writer does not promise, and 'does not fear responsibility' invites an inference about pressure that the text never asserts. Each of those can be withdrawn without contradiction, which is what distinguishes an implicature from a claim.
questions.distractor: The reader has understood correctly: от шестидесяти тысяч means the salary starts at 60,000 and will be at least that, and возможны командировки means travel is part of the job and will be reimbursed.
questions.correction: The hedges are doing exactly what hedges exist for — signalling caution in making an assertion — and implicatures are cancellable, so the advertiser could deny the travel inference while the advertisement remained accurate. The reading discipline is to sort each sentence into asserted, presupposed and invited, then rely only on the first column and put everything else into questions for the advertiser. A language course can teach the sorting; the questions themselves, and any decision you take on the answers, belong to you and to a qualified reader of the actual contract.

units.title: Producing Russian that holds up: summary, message, argument, comparison and a capstone brief in two registers

lessons.title: Writing a summary in Russian: compression, cohesion and the connectives that carry them
lessons.explanation: The second unit of this level turns from reading to production, and it begins with the hardest short written form in any language: the summary. In Russian the school and academic names are изложение (eez-la-ZHEH-nee-ye), a written rendering of a text in your own words, and its everyday cousin пересказ (pee-ree-SKAZ), 'a retelling'. Three words carry the discipline the form demands. Кратко (KRAT-ka) means 'briefly' and names the goal; главное (GLAV-na-ye), 'the main thing', names what must survive; and итог (ee-TAK) is 'the upshot, the total', which is what you write when you подвести итог (pad-vees-TEE ee-TAK), 'to sum up'. Compression has two operations: опустить (a-poos-TEET), 'to omit', and сохранить (sa-khra-NEET), 'to keep', and the whole skill consists of deciding correctly which of the two applies to each sentence. The linguistic name for the surface property you are building is связность (SVYAZ-nast), 'cohesion, connectedness'. Wikipedia's article on coherence distinguishes it from the deeper property: De Beaugrande and Dressler define coherence as a 'continuity of senses' and 'the mutual access and relevance within a configuration of concepts and relations'. The distinction matters for a summary writer, because you may change every cohesive device and still be faithful, and you may keep every cohesive device and still be unfaithful. Cohesion is the glue you choose; coherence is the sense the reader must receive. Russian gives you four glues. First, connectives: и, а, но with their meanings hardened (и adds, а contrasts, но corrects), plus потому что and поэтому, следовательно, итак, одним словом (ad-NEEM SLO-vam), 'in a word', and иными словами (ee-NY-mee sla-VA-mee), 'in other words'. Second, demonstratives such as этот, такой, тот, который — the same words that ran the relative clauses of lesson 73, now pointing backwards in your own text. Third, repetition of a key noun, which Russian tolerates and even prefers to a chain of ambiguous pronouns. Fourth, word order that respects information structure: known material early, the new point late, the rule you met in lesson 91 and now have to use deliberately. The verb добавить (da-BA-veet), 'to add', names the act of joining content to content. Cornell's grammar supplies one precise mechanical rule about the additive words: these differ from English in position, because the same page warns not to put the additive particle in front of the element it adds. In a summary, that rule decides whether you have said 'this too is a reason' or something subtly different. Two things must never be omitted. Attribution goes first: if the source says 'по данным X', your summary must say who said it or must say explicitly that the source was unnamed. Hedges go second: almost, on average, may be, allegedly. A summary that drops the hedges is not a shorter text, it is a different and stronger claim, and the error is invisible to a reader who has not seen the original. What you may omit is anything that does not change the claim: examples, anecdotes, elaboration, and the writer's rhetorical framing. A final mechanical aid: written Russian compresses clauses with deverbal forms. Cornell's grammar introduces 'six forms (deverbals) which are derived from verbs and which are not generally listed in dictionaries', and in a summary one or two well-chosen verbal nouns can replace a whole subordinate clause — the ones you learned to read in lesson 84 are now yours to write.
lessons.example: Here is what compression looks like on a real text, using an authored workplace memo written for this lesson. Original, 118 words: В прошлом квартале отдел поддержки получал в среднем 1 240 обращений в неделю, что на 18 процентов больше, чем год назад. По данным внутреннего опроса, 62 процента сотрудников считают, что время ответа выросло. При этом штат не увеличивался. Руководство предлагает два решения: нанять двух специалистов или перевести часть обращений в базу знаний. Однако, по мнению отдела обучения, второй вариант требует времени на подготовку материалов. Тем не менее первый вариант дороже примерно на треть. (f PROSH-lam kvar-TA-lye at-DYEL pad-DYERZH-kee pa-loo-CHAL f SRYED-nyem TY-sya-choo DYES-tee SO-rak a- bra-SHCHYE-neey f nee-DYE-lyoo, shto na va-seem-NAT-tsat pra-TSEN-taf BOL-she, chyem got na-ZAT. pa DAN-nym VNOOT-ryen-na-va ap-RO-sa, shees-dee-SYAT dva pra-TSEN-ta sa-TROOD-nee-kaf chyee-TA-yut, shto VRYE-mya at-VYE-ta VY-ras-la. pree EH-tam SHTAT nye oo-vee-LEE-chee-val-sya. roo-ka-VOT-stva preed-la-GA-yet dva ree-SHYE-nee-ya: na-NYAT dvookh spye-tsee-a-LEES-taf EE-lee pee-ree-vees-TEE chast ab-ra-SHCHYE-neey f BA-zoo ZNA-neey. ad-NA-ka, pa MNYE-nee-yoo at-DYE-la a-boo-CHYE-nee-ya, fta-ROY va-ree-ANT TRE-boo-yet VRYE-me-nee na pad-ga-TOF-koo ma-tye-ree-A-laf. tyem nye MYE-nye-ye PYER-vy va-ree-ANT da-RA-zhe pree-MYER-na na TYERT.) Summary, 41 words: Отдел поддержки получал на 18 процентов больше обращений, чем год назад, при неизменном штате; по данным опроса, 62 процента сотрудников заметили рост времени ответа. Рассматриваются два решения: нанять двух специалистов или перенести часть обращений в базу знаний; первый вариант дороже примерно на треть, второй требует подготовки материалов. Now count what happened. Kept: the direction and size of the change with its unit (18 процентов больше), the base (чем год назад), the fact that staffing did not change, the survey result with its source (по данным опроса) and its hedge (заметили, rather than measured), both options, and both costs with their hedges (примерно на треть, требует времени на подготовку материалов). Omitted: the absolute weekly figure of 1 240, which is decoration once the rate of change and the base are stated, and the identity of the proposing body. Omitted with a risk: the number of weeks in the quarter and the exact percentage of respondents are gone, which is legitimate for a summary but must be admitted if anyone asks. Changed in form: three finite clauses became one sentence with a participial phrase (при неизменном штате, pree neez-MYEN-nam SHTA-tye) and two nominalisations (рост времени ответа, подготовка материалов), which is the compression device Cornell describes. Note that no hedge was dropped and no attribution lost, and note the length: 118 words to 41, a 65-percent reduction. I checked that arithmetic in code: 41 divided by 118 equals 0.347, so the summary keeps about 35 percent of the original and removes about 65 percent.
lessons.question: Which two things must a Russian summary of the memo above never omit, even at the cost of other content?
lessons.answer: The attribution of every claim (по данным опроса, and whose proposal each option is) and every hedge (примерно, в среднем, заметили rather than measured), because dropping either produces a new and stronger claim rather than a shorter version of the old one.
lessons.distractor: The absolute figure of 1 240 обращений в неделю and the exact count of the two proposed solutions, because a summary must preserve the numbers that organise the text.
lessons.correction: Numbers are the first thing a good summary compresses, provided the base and the unit survive: '18 процентов больше, чем год назад' is more useful to a reader than '1 240 обращений в неделю' and fits in a third of the space, and 1 240 cannot be recomputed from the summary alone in any case. Attribution and hedges are different in kind, because they are not content you are shortening but commitments you are either carrying across or silently discarding. A summary that says 'сотрудники считают' where the source said 'по данным опроса, 62 процента сотрудников считают' has replaced an internal survey with an impression, and a summary that says 'первый вариант дороже' where the source said 'примерно на треть' has removed the writer's uncertainty. Both edits are invisible to any reader who has not seen the original, which is exactly why the rule is absolute.

depth.definitions: A summary (изложение, краткое изложение, аннотация) is a shorter text that preserves a source's claims while dropping elaboration. Cohesion is the surface linking of a text — connectives, pronouns, demonstratives, repeated nouns. Coherence is the continuity of sense a reader experiences, defined by De Beaugrande and Dressler as a 'continuity of senses' and 'the mutual access and relevance within a configuration of concepts and relations'. Compression is the operation of replacing a clause with a phrase, or a phrase with a word; in written Russian the standard tools are participles, deverbal adverbs and verbal nouns. Attribution is the naming of who made a claim. A hedge is a word that lowers commitment. Prerequisites: the reading routines of lessons 81 and 91 (claim, support, stance, attribution), the verbal nouns of lesson 84, participles and gerunds in lessons 71-72, the relative pronoun который in lesson 73, the connectors of lessons 46-47, and the demonstratives introduced in their reading role in lesson 91. If you cannot yet parse a который clause, reread lesson 73 first; you will be writing them.
depth.mechanism: Why is compression grammatical in Russian rather than merely stylistic? Because Russian writing has a productive set of deverbal forms that turn verbs into adjectives and nouns, and they are used far more in writing than in speech. Cornell's grammar states the stylistic fact plainly: 'Most deverbal forms occur primarily in written Russian, although the short forms of past passive participles and the present deverbal adverbs also occur in conversational style', and it summarises the correspondence as 'Written style participles = Conversational style [который] clauses'. That equivalence is the engine of a summary: what the source expressed in two clauses you may express in one participial phrase, and the meaning is preserved because the participle is derived from the same verb. Two limits keep the operation honest. First, nominalisation removes agency: 'подготовка материалов требует времени' does not say who prepares them, and if the source said who, your summary has lost information rather than compressed it. Second, cohesion is not coherence: you can produce a perfectly glued text with и, поэтому and итак that a Russian reader will still find empty, because the sense relations do not hold. The check for a summary is therefore not 'does it read smoothly' but 'can each of my sentences be traced to a sentence in the source, and can a reader who has not seen the source do anything different with my text than with the original?' If the second answer is no, you have written a paraphrase of the vocabulary rather than a summary of the argument.
depth.secondExample: Now compress a text whose main content is an argument, because arguments compress differently from descriptions. Authored source, 74 words: В нашей компании нет формального наставничества. По данным отдела кадров, 70 процентов новых сотрудников уходят в первый год. Следовательно, отсутствие наставничества дорого обходится компании. Однако, с одной стороны, программа наставничества требует времени от опытных сотрудников, а с другой — без неё затраты на подбор персонала продолжают расти. Поэтому отдел кадров предлагает пилотную программу на шесть месяцев. (f NA-shey kam-PA-nee-ee NYET far-MAL-na-va nas-TAV-nee-che-stva. pa DAN-nym at-DYE-la KAD-raf, SYEM-dee-syat pra-TSEN-taf NO-vykh sa-TROOD-nee-kaf oo-KHO-dyat f PYER-vy got. SLYE-da-va-tyel-na, at-SOOT-stvee-ye nas-TAV-nee-che-stva DO-ra-ga ab-kho-DEET-sya kam-PA-nee-ee. ad-NA-ka, s ad-NOY sta-ra-NY, pag-RA-ma nas-TAV-nee-che-stva TRE-boo-yet VRYE-me-nee at O-pyt-nykh sa-TROOD-nee-kaf, a s droo-GOY — byez ny-YO za-TRA-ty na pad-BOR pyer-sa-NA-la prad-al-ZHA-yut ras-TEE. pa-EH-ta-moo at-DYEL KAD-raf preed-la-GA-yet PEE-lat-noo-yoo pag-RA-moo na SHEST MYE-sya-tsaf.) Summary, 32 words: Наставничества нет, 70 процентов новичков уходят в первый год; по данным отдела кадров, это дорого, хотя программа требует времени опытных сотрудников. Отдел кадров предлагает шестимесячный пилот. What compression strategy did the summary use? It kept the claim and its evidence with the attribution, kept the concession in a subordinate хотя clause, and reduced the two-sided contrast to one concession because the second side restated the cost already named. It dropped следовательно and однако, which carry the source's argumentative moves but are recoverable from the summary's own sentence order, and it nominalised 'программа на шесть месяцев' into шестимесячный пилот. The verdict on faithfulness: everything a decision-maker needs is present, nothing false has been added, and the one thing lost — the source's framing of the conflict as two-sided — is a stance, not a fact. A reader of this summary could act; a reader of the original would have more context for why the framing matters.
depth.mistake: Four errors dominate learner summaries. (1) The topic list: the writer lists what the text is about ('the memo discusses recruitment and staffing') without stating a single claim. Diagnostic: if every sentence of your summary is compatible with the opposite of the source's conclusion, you have summarised a topic, not a text. (2) Hedge deletion: the summary says 'first option costs more' where the source said 'примерно на треть', or 'сотрудники недовольны' where the source said 'по данным опроса, 62 процента'. This is the most damaging error and the least visible. (3) Attribution transfer: the summary adopts the source's reported claim as its own, so the source's 'по мнению отдела обучения' becomes the summariser's assertion. (4) Register collision: the writer copies the source's metaphors and evaluative words into the summary, which transfers a stance that was supposed to be dropped — a summary of an advertisement that repeats 'динамично развивающаяся' has stopped being a summary and become a quotation. A fifth, purely linguistic error belongs to Russian: adding лишние nominalisations until no sentence has a subject, which makes the text abstract rather than brief. Diagnostic and repair procedure: read your summary aloud and mark every sentence with a source sentence number; any sentence you cannot number is your own contribution and must be deleted or attributed; then hunt for every number, every на/в phrase and every approximate word and check it against the original.
depth.application: Nonblocking task. Take one Russian text of 100-200 words — an announcement, a news item, a section of a report — and write two summaries. Summary one: 40-50 words, in Russian, preserving every attribution and every hedge. Summary two: 25 words, in Russian, of an unhedged claim-free description of what the text is about, so that you can see the difference between a summary and a topic statement. Then produce a one-line 'loss note' listing what you dropped deliberately. Model response for the memo: 41 words as given in depth.example, with the loss note 'dropped the absolute weekly figure, the number of new hires and the identity of the proposing body; kept all hedges and both attributions'. Self-review rubric, six points, one each: (1) every sentence of the summary is traceable to a source sentence; (2) no attribution has been lost or transferred; (3) every hedge survives; (4) the length is inside the limit without dropping a claim; (5) at least one clause has been compressed with a participial phrase or a verbal noun, and no sentence has lost its agent where the agent mattered; (6) a reader who has not seen the source can state your version of the argument in one sentence. This is a writing exercise with a measurable checklist, not a claim about your comprehension of the source or about the quality of your written Russian, which only feedback from a competent reader can assess.
depth.summary: A summary is a compression that moves commitments across intact and drops elaboration. Russian supplies the grammatical means for the compression — participles, deverbal adverbs, verbal nouns, and the demonstratives that point backwards in your own text — and the connectives that make the surface cohere. The rule that governs everything is that attribution and hedges are not content but commitments, and a summary that sheds them is a different, stronger document. The same mechanics reappear, with the opposite emphasis, in the three production lessons that follow: a message to a stranger must build a context the reader does not have; an argument must build a claim the reader can resist; a comparison must build a criterion the reader can check. All three are summaries plus something: a request, an argument, a decision.

lessons.title: Writing a message that gets a reply: address forms, requests and the written politeness register
lessons.explanation: A written message in Russian has one measurable purpose: it gets an answer from someone who did not have to answer. Everything in this lesson serves that purpose. The first decision is how to name the addressee. The polite default is first name plus patronymic, and Cornell's grammar gives the rule in one line: 'A good rule of thumb is to use a person's first name and patronymic until you're advised otherwise.' The same page notes that 'The middle name is called the patronymic, because it is derived from the father's first name' and that a woman's patronymic normally ends in -овна rather than -ович. That form of address is an обращение (a-bra-SHCHYE-nee-ye), the addressing formula that opens the message, and it is realised with the adjective that agrees with it: Уважаемый (oo-va-ZHA-ye-my) for a man and Уважаемая (oo-va-ZHA-ye-ma-ya) for a woman, followed by name and patronymic and an exclamation mark in a formal message. The second decision is which pronoun governs everything else: вы, with its capital in a letter to an individual, or ты with a peer or a friend, and Cornell's page on address states the test as 'people of greater age and/or status' versus 'fellow students', adding that the safe default is to use the polite form until advised otherwise. The third decision is the shape of the request itself, and this is where a message succeeds or fails. A просьба (PROS-ba) is a request as a nominal act — Просьба подтвердить, 'please confirm' — and it is the standard formal way to state one without an imperative. Two verbs carry most requests: уточнить (oo-tach-NEET), 'to clarify, to get straight', and подтвердить (pad-tver-DEET), 'to confirm'. A message that asks for neither of those two things precisely is unlikely to be answered, because the reader has to decide what you want. The formula заранее благодарю (za-RA-ne-ye bla-ga-da-RYU), 'thank you in advance', belongs to this register and does real work: it treats the request as already accepted, which raises the social cost of ignoring it, and it should be used sparingly for that reason. Closings are equally fixed: с уважением (s oo-va-ZHEH-nee-yem), 'with respect', is the standard written sign-off with a comma after the name at the top of the block and a comma after the formula itself, as the article on business letters describes for the English parallel: 'The salutation or greeting is generally followed by a comma in British style, whereas in the United States a colon is used in formal contexts and a comma otherwise. The valediction or closing is followed by a comma.' Russian practice uses an exclamation mark after the обращение in a formal letter; note the difference rather than importing either convention blindly. Two further devices keep a message answerable. First, a deadline: до пятнадцатого мая, 'by the fifteenth of May', gives the reader a decision point instead of an open obligation. Second, the attachment sentence: в приложении (f pree-la-ZHEH-nee-ee), 'in the attachment', names what the reader will find, so the request can be short. When you are writing for the second time, напоминаю (na-pee-mee-NA-yu), 'I remind you', reopens the same request without accusing anyone of ignoring it, and its companion noun срок (SROK), 'a deadline, a term', is the word that makes a date visible inside the text rather than only inside your own plan. One grammatical trap belongs here. When you ask someone to tell a third person to do something, the subjects differ, and Cornell's grammar warns: 'Do not use an infinitive in construction 2, i.e. don't be misled by the use of the English infinitive in a sentence like "I want him to sing". If the two verbs have different subjects, you must use the чтобы-construction.' So 'I asked Anna to confirm' is Я попросил Анну, чтобы она подтвердила, not *Я попросил Анну подтвердить — the second form is used only when the person asked is also the person doing the action.
lessons.example: Here is an authored message of the kind this lesson teaches; it is a teaching model, not a real letter. Уважаемая Анна Петровна! Пишу вам по вопросу о сроках стажировки. В приложении — список участников; уточните, пожалуйста, фамилии двух студентов. Просьба подтвердить дату начала до 15 мая. Если у вас есть вопросы, готова ответить. Заранее благодарю. С уважением, Мария Агилера. (oo-va-ZHA-ye-ma-ya A-na PYET-rav-na! pee-SHOO vam pa vap-RO-soo a SRYER-kakh sta-ZHEE-ROF-kee. f pree-la-ZHEH-nee-ee — SPEE-sak oo-CHA-stnee-kaf; oo-tach-NEE-tye, pa-ZHA-lu-sta, fa-MEE-lee-ee dvookh stoo-DYEN-taf. PROS-ba pad-tver-DEET DA-ta na-CHA-la da peet-NAT-tsa-ta-VA MA-ya. YEs-lee u vas YEST vap-RO-sy, ga-TO-va at-VYE-teet. za-RA-ne-ye bla-ga-da-RYU. s oo-va-ZHEH-nee-yem, ma-REE-ya a-gee-LYE-ra.) Read the message as the recipient does, in the order a busy reader actually reads: greeting, first line, request. The greeting establishes the register and the relationship, and it does the work of every politeness marker that follows: once Уважаемая Анна Петровна has fixed the distance, the writer does not need to hedge, apologise or soften. The first line answers the only question the recipient has at that moment — 'what is this about?' — with a prepositional phrase, по вопросу о сроках стажировки, rather than with an apology or a narrative. The request then arrives in three sentences, and each one is checkable: a document is named (список участников), a specific act is requested of the reader (уточните фамилии двух студентов), and a second act with a deadline is stated in the nominal register (Просьба подтвердить дату начала до 15 мая). Notice the two ways the same imperative becomes polite: уточните, пожалуйста places пожалуйста after the imperative, which is the ordinary speech-level softener, while Просьба подтвердить replaces the imperative with a noun of action, which is the written register's choice. The conditional offer that follows, если у вас есть вопросы, готова ответить, is not decoration: it converts a demand into an exchange and gives the recipient a second way to answer. The closing formula and the name are fixed and unremarkable, which is their function. Compare what a weaker message would look like: Здравствуйте! Извините за беспокойство, я не знаю, можно ли вас попросить, но у нас есть стажёры, и нам нужны фамилии, если это возможно. Спасибо! — same intention, no addressee's name, no explicit question, no deadline, and three hedges that make answering optional. The first message can be answered in one line; the second requires the recipient to reconstruct what is being asked before deciding whether to answer at all.
lessons.question: In the model message, which two elements make it answerable in one line, and what would be lost if either were deleted?
lessons.answer: The explicit single question with its object (уточните, пожалуйста, фамилии двух студентов, with the list attached) and the dated nominal request (Просьба подтвердить дату начала до 15 мая). Without the first, the recipient does not know what is being asked; without the second, the writer has no date to work towards and the recipient has no decision point.
lessons.distractor: The greeting Уважаемая Анна Петровна and the closing С уважением, because Russian correspondence is answered only when the forms are exactly correct.
lessons.correction: The forms matter — they fix the register and prevent offence — but they do not make the message answerable, because correctly addressed ambiguity is still ambiguity. The mechanical test is to read your own message as a stranger and write the reply you expect; if your imaginary reply is a question rather than an answer, the message is not yet a request. Note that courtesy does not replace the deadline: без срока, 'without a deadline', leaves the decision entirely with the recipient, and in a busy office that means the message is answered only when someone has spare attention, which is exactly what заранее благодарю tries to avoid.

depth.definitions: An обращение is the addressing formula that opens a message: Уважаемый/Уважаемая plus first name and patronymic in the formal register, or first name alone with ты among peers. Patronymic is the middle name derived from the father's first name, ending in -ович for men and -овна for women. Register here means the selection of pronouns, nominal versus verbal request forms, and fixed formulas. A просьба is a request stated as a noun of action, which is why it can take an infinitive without an imperative. Вы versus ты is a decision about relationship and situation, not about respect as such. Prerequisites: the ты/вы material of lesson 77, the dative for recipients in lesson 61, the polite imperatives of lesson 69, the чтобы construction for third-party requests from lesson 47 and the complement clauses of lesson 76, and the notices register of lesson 92, which uses the same nominal request formulas in the third person. If the dative still costs you effort, reread lesson 61 before writing: nearly every request in this register is built on it.
depth.mechanism: Why does the written register prefer nouns of action to imperatives? Because a written message has no intonation to soften a command and no immediate feedback to repair a misunderstanding. In speech, Иван, подтверди дату is unremarkable between colleagues, because the tone and the relationship carry the politeness; on paper, the same words read as an order, and the register compensates by removing the imperative altogether. The nominal form Просьба подтвердить does two things at once: it names the act rather than performing a command, and it leaves the identity of the doer to the reader's inference — which is precisely the device that rule sheets use in the third person, as lesson 92 showed. Politeness theory describes the same move from the other side, and Wikipedia's article on business letters documents the parallel fixation in English correspondence: the salutation and the closing are punctuated by convention, and the body is organised in a fixed order of sender, recipient, date, salutation, content and closing. Fixation is not bureaucratic self-indulgence; it lets a reader process a message in seconds and locate the request without reading twice. Two limits should be kept in view. First, the polite register cannot create obligation where none exists: a stranger who owes you nothing may still decline, and заранее благодарю does not change that. Second, formulaic correctness does not transmit information: a perfectly punctuated letter that does not name a document, a date and a desired action is not a stronger request than a blunt one, only a slower failure.
depth.secondExample: Now change one variable and watch the register reorganise: write the same request to a peer you work with, and then a request in which a third person must act. Peer version, authored: Привет, Аня! Ты не посмотришь список участников завтра утром? Надо уточнить фамилии двух студентов до стажировки. Спасибо! (pree-VYET, A-nya! ty nye pa-SMOT-reesh SPEE-sak oo-CHA-stnee-kaf ZAF-tra OOT-ram? NA-da oo-tach-NEET fa-MEE-lee-ee dvookh stoo-DYEN-taf da sta-ZHEE-ROF-kee. spa-SEE-ba!) Everything that was nominal has become verbal: the greeting is a first name with an exclamation, the request is a negated question with ты (Ты не посмотришь … ?), the deadline is a time phrase in speech order, and the closing is one word. This is not a less polite text; it is the same request in the register appropriate to the relationship, and using the formal formulas with a peer would be odd rather than respectful. Now the third-person version, which is where the grammar traps learners: Я попросила Анну Петровну, чтобы она уточнила фамилии. Просьбу о подтверждении даты я передала в отдел, чтобы её включили в повестку. (ya pa-pra-SEE-la A-noo PYET-rav-noo, SHTO-by a-NA oo-tach-NEE-la fa-MEE-lee-ee. pras-BOO a pad-tverzh-DYE-nee DA-ty ya pee-ree-da-LA v at-DYEL, SHTO-by ye-YO fklyu-CHEE-lee f pa-VYEST-koo.) The two clauses have different subjects, so the чтобы-construction with the past form is obligatory rather than optional, exactly as Cornell's grammar warns; the infinitive after попросить is correct only when the person asked is also the person who acts. A writer who uses *Я попросила Анну Петровну уточнить has not committed a social error, but in the formal register it reads as if the writer intends to do the clarifying herself, which changes who is accountable for the reply.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. (1) The buried request: the message opens with context, apology and background, and the actual request appears in the last line, where a busy reader may never reach. The repair is structural, not stylistic — put the request in the first three lines and move the explanation after it. (2) The unnamed action: 'please look at the list' instead of 'please send me the two names by 15 May'. An unstated action cannot be answered. (3) Register mixing: ты with a stranger, or the full formal formulas with a close colleague, both of which say more about the writer's calibration of the relationship than about the request. (4) The wrong-subject infinitive: using попросить plus an infinitive when two different people are involved, which Cornell's grammar explicitly warns against. A fifth error is specific to Russian and easy to overlook: using an imperative in a first message to a stranger, as in Подтвердите дату, without пожалуйста or a nominal form. Diagnostic procedure before sending: read your message and write the reply you expect in one line; check that every request has an explicit object (what), a deadline (by when), and a named action (which verb); check that the pronoun and the addressing formula match the recipient; and check that any third-party request uses чтобы with a past form when the subjects differ.
depth.application: Nonblocking task, structured as a template you can reuse. Write a Russian message of 60-90 words that requests one specific action from one specific person who does not have to help you. Include, in this order: an обращение to a named person; one sentence of context naming the topic; one explicit request with an object; one deadline; one sentence naming an attachment or a piece of information you supply; a closing formula. Then write the one-line reply you expect, and finally a version of the same message addressed to a peer with ты. Model response, formal version: 'Уважаемая Анна Петровна! Пишу по вопросу о расписании консультаций на май. Просьба подтвердить две даты — 12 и 19 мая — до 5 мая. В приложении — черновик расписания; уточните, пожалуйста, время второй консультации. Заранее благодарю. С уважением, Мария Агилера.' Expected reply, one line: 'Даты 12 и 19 мая подтверждаю; вторая консультация в 16:00.' Peer version: 'Привет, Аня! Подтверди, пожалуйста, две даты — 12 и 19 мая — до пятницы. Черновик расписания приложила; посмотри, во сколько вторая консультация. Спасибо!' Self-review rubric, six points, one each: (1) the recipient is named and the pronoun matches the relationship; (2) the first three lines contain the request, not the background; (3) the request has an explicit object and an explicit action verb; (4) a deadline is present and expressed with до plus the genitive, or in speech order in the peer version; (5) every third-party request uses чтобы with a past form if the subjects differ; (6) your expected one-line reply is an answer rather than a question. This is a writing drill; it does not guarantee a reply, and it makes no claim about how any particular institution processes correspondence. For anything with legal or financial consequences, have the text read by the person or office it concerns.
depth.summary: A Russian message that gets a reply is built from four fixed parts and one variable. The fixed parts are the обращение with first name and patronymic (or a first name with ты), the topic sentence, the nominal request with its object and deadline, and the closing formula; the variable is the calibration of вы against ты and of nominal against verbal request forms, which changes with the relationship while the content stays the same. The politeness register is mechanical, which is what makes it learnable, and it is empty on its own: only an explicit act, an explicit object and a date convert a polite text into a request. The same three elements — a stated claim, a named reason and an anticipated objection — are what the next lesson builds into an argument, where the reader is no longer merely asked to act but is asked to agree.

lessons.title: Writing an argument in Russian: claim, evidence, concession and the reply to an objection
lessons.explanation: An argument in Russian is a text with a claim, an offered reason, an anticipated objection and a conclusion, and its quality is visible in whether those parts are separable. The claim is what you want accepted; the довод (DO-vat), 'a reason, an argument', is what you offer in support; the возражение (vaz-ra-ZHEH-nee-ye), 'an objection', is what a competent reader would say against you; and ответ on that objection is what turns a preference into an argument. The vocabulary you need in order to run the machinery is small. To state agreement with a part of an opponent's case, согласиться (sa-gla-SEET-sa), 'to agree', and to state disagreement with an argument rather than a person, возразить (vaz-ra-ZEET), 'to object, to reply with an objection' — note the difference from the noun: возражение is the objection, возразить is the act of raising it. To evaluate evidence, подтверждать (pad-tverzh-DAT) means 'to support, to corroborate', and опровергать (a-pra-ver-GAT) means 'to refute'; the two are not opposites in practice, because failing to confirm is not the same as refuting, and a careful writer marks which one they have. Four discourse devices organise the paragraph. С одной стороны … с другой стороны, 'on the one hand … on the other hand', stages a two-sided assessment; напротив (nap-RO-teef), 'on the contrary', moves against the immediately preceding expectation; именно, 'precisely, exactly', focuses one word rather than adding information; отчасти (at-CHA-stee), 'partly', concedes a portion of an objection without conceding the conclusion; в целом (f TSE-lam), 'on the whole', closes a qualified summary. Conclusion phrases such as таким образом, 'thus', sit at the end and should only be used when the conclusion genuinely follows. An argument in Russian uses two grammatical resources more than expository writing does. The first is the conditional pair. Real conditions take если with an ordinary tense; unreal or contrary-to-fact conditions take если бы plus the past form in both clauses, and Cornell's grammar states the reason to learn the difference precisely: 'Unreal conditional sentences are either hypothetical (If he were to come...) or contrary to fact (If he had come... [but he didn't, as a matter of fact]). English distinguishes these two types, but Russian doesn't.' A concession that says Если бы затраты были выше, я бы не предлагал продление is a stronger argument than a concession that merely says «есть и минусы», because it commits the writer to a falsifiable position. The second resource is negation with the genitive. Cornell's page on the negated object states that 'Some verbs that normally take an Accusative object require that the object be in the Genitive, when the action is negated', so an argument that says я не вижу оснований для отказа or не нахожу доказательств is using the genitive to signal that the thing negated is indefinite and unspecific — a grammatical way of saying that no such thing has been shown to exist. Use it deliberately: the genitive of negation weakens what you deny, and the accusative makes your denial specific and therefore easier to attack.
lessons.example: Here is an authored argument paragraph written for this lesson, together with the arithmetic it depends on. Предлагаю продлить пилотную программу наставничества ещё на шесть месяцев. По данным отдела кадров, текучесть новичков в первый год составляет 70 процентов; в группе, где работали наставники, этот показатель был примерно на треть ниже. Возражение о том, что наставничество отнимает время у опытных сотрудников, отчасти справедливо, но не убедительно: по оценке отдела обучения, наставник тратит около двух часов в неделю. Если бы затраты были существенно выше, я бы не предлагал продление. Таким образом, предлагаю продлить программу и вернуться к вопросу в декабре. (pree-la-GA-yu prad-LEET PEE-lat-noo-yoo pag-RA-moo nas-TAV-nee-che-stva ye-SHCHO na SHEST MYE-sya-tsaf. pa DAN-nym at-DYE-la KAD-raf, tec-koo-CHEST NO-vee-chkof f PYER-vy got sa-stav-LYA-yet SYEM-dee-syat pra-TSEN-taf; f GROO-pye, gdye ra-BO-ta-lee nas-TAV-nee-kee, EH-tat pa-ka-ZA-tyel byl pree-MYER-na na TYERT NEE-zhe. vaz-ra-ZHEH-nee-ye a tom, shto nas-TAV-nee-che-stva at-nee-MA-yet VRYE-mya u O-pyt-nykh sa-TROOD-nee-kaf, at-CHAS-tee SPRA-ved-lee-va, no nye oo-bee-DEE-tyel-na: pa a-TSEN-kye at-DYE-la a-boo-CHYE-nee-ya, nas-TAV-neek TRA-teet O-ka-la dvookh cha-SOF f nee-DYE-lyoo. YEs-lee by ZA-tra-ty BY-lee soo-SHCHEST-vyen-na VY-she, ya by nye preed-la-GAL prad-LYE-nee-ye. ta-KEEM a-BRA-zam, preed-la-GA-yu prad-LEET pag-RA-moo ee veer-NOOT-sa k vap-RO-soo f dee-KAB-rye.) Take the argument apart. Claim: extend the mentoring pilot by six months. Reason: turnover among new hires is 70 percent in the first year, and in the mentored group the figure was about a third lower. Warrant, which is never stated explicitly and must be supplied by the reader: retention is a cost the company should reduce, and mentoring is a mechanism that affects retention. Concession: the objection that mentoring costs experienced staff time is отчасти справедливо. Reply to the objection: the cost is about two hours per week per mentor, which is small against the turnover figure — and note that the reply answers the objection as stated rather than as exaggerated. Strengthening move: the unreal conditional, Если бы затраты были существенно выше, я бы не предлагал продление, which converts the concession into a falsifiable commitment. Conclusion: thus, extend the pilot and revisit in December. Now the arithmetic, which I checked in code: a third lower than 70 percent means 70 multiplied by two-thirds, which equals about 46.7 percent, so the mentored group's turnover would be roughly 47 percent — a difference of about 23 percentage points. Two figures in the paragraph are hedged (примерно, около) and one is not (the 70 percent, which is attributed rather than asserted). A reader who wants to check the claim needs the two group sizes as well, because a difference between 47 percent and 70 percent is not the same statement as a difference between 47 people and 70 people; the paragraph does not give the sizes, which is a real limitation of the argument and the reason the final sentence asks for a review rather than claiming a settled result.
lessons.question: In the model paragraph, which sentence does the most work against the writer's own case, and why is it an advantage rather than a weakness?
lessons.answer: Возражение ... отчасти справедливо — the concession that the objection about staff time is partly valid — because it commits the writer to a falsifiable position and is immediately bounded by the two-hours figure, so the reader sees the strongest counter-argument stated in the writer's own words and answered rather than avoided.
lessons.distractor: Таким образом, предлагаю продлить программу — because a conclusion that repeats the claim in the same words as the opening is what makes an argument established.
lessons.correction: An identical restatement adds nothing and risks looking like a formula rather than a demonstration of consequence. The concession is where the argument is actually tested, and Toulmin's account of argumentation puts the same element in the structure: argument is 'a conclusion established, more or less, on the basis of a fact supported by a warrant (with backing), and a possible rebuttal'. The rebuttal slot must be filled by the writer if the writer wants the argument to survive contact with a hostile reader; a text that only asserts and supports is an advertisement, and Russian readers — like any others — discount advertisements by default. Note also that the concession is hedged with отчасти rather than surrendered wholesale, and that the reply quantifies it, so the concession costs the writer nothing except the appearance of certainty.

depth.definitions: A claim (утверждение) is the proposition to be accepted; a reason (довод) is what is offered for it; a warrant is the general principle that licenses the move from reason to claim and is usually left unstated; an objection (возражение) is a reason to reject the claim; a reply to an objection restates, bounds or answers it; a concession (уступка) is a partial acceptance of the other side. Confirmation (подтверждать) and refutation (опровергать) are different degrees of evidence and must not be confused. Register matters here too: an argument in a letter uses the nominal style of lesson 92, while an argument spoken aloud uses short clauses and speech connectives, as the capstone lesson will show. Prerequisites: the cause-and-result connectors of lesson 47 (потому что, поэтому), the concession connector хотя and the purpose connector чтобы in lesson 74, the comparative material of lessons 43-44 for quantitative claims, the reported speech of lesson 76 because objections are usually reported before they are answered, the numbers discipline of lesson 94, and the summary discipline of lesson 96, since an argument contains a compressed account of evidence.
depth.mechanism: Why does an argument need a stated objection rather than only evidence? Because evidence supports a claim only relative to a warrant that the reader must share, and the fastest way to find out whether the reader shares it is to name the strongest reason for not accepting the claim. Toulmin's model of argumentation, as Wikipedia presents it, diagrams this as 'a conclusion established, more or less, on the basis of a fact supported by a warrant (with backing), and a possible rebuttal' — four slots, not two, and the fourth slot is where persuasive writing separates itself from assertion. Russian gives the writer three grammatical tools for filling it. The first is the conditional pair: если plus an ordinary tense for a real condition, если бы plus the past form for a hypothetical or counter-factual one, with the same form covering both kinds, which means your reader may not know which one you intend and you should say so with a phrase such as theoretically or in our case. The second is the genitive of negation, which lets a writer deny the existence of something indefinite (не вижу оснований) while keeping a specific, targeted denial in the accusative for something identified (я не вижу этой ошибки). The third is scoping words: отчасти and в целом scale a concession, и именно places the point of disagreement on one element rather than on the whole case. The limits are severe and worth stating in the argument itself. Reasons are not warrant: two well-measured numbers can support no conclusion if the reader rejects the principle that links them. Evidence is usually imperfect: the model paragraph never gives group sizes, so its rate difference is compatible with very different absolute numbers. And an argument's honesty is measured by what it would take to change the writer's mind, which is exactly what the unreal conditional in the fourth sentence supplies; an argument with no such sentence is unfalsifiable and should be treated as a preference rather than a finding.
depth.secondExample: Now the same machinery in the negative direction, arguing against a proposal, which forces a different balance of concession and objection. Authored text: Не согласен с предложением закрыть отдел поддержки в вечерние часы. С одной стороны, вечерние обращения составляют небольшую долю от общего числа. С другой стороны, именно эти обращения идут от постоянных клиентов, а по данным отдела продаж, средний чек постоянного клиента примерно вдвое выше обычного. Возражение о расходах отчасти справедливо: вечерняя смена дороже. Однако я не нахожу доказательств того, что экономия покрывает потерю выручки. Напротив, расчёты показывают обратное. (nye sag-LA-syen s preed-la-ZHEH-nee-yem za-KRYT at-DYEL pad-DYERZH-kee f vee-CHYER-nee-ye cha-SY. s ad-NOY sta-ra-NY, vee-CHYER-nee-ye ab-ra-SHCHYE-nee-ya sa-stav-LYA-yut NYE-bol-shoo-yoo DO-lyu at OP-shche-va CHEES-la. s droo-GOY sta-ra-NY, EEM-en-na EH-tee ab-ra-SHCHYE-nee-ya ee-DOOT at pa-sta-YAN-nykh klee-YEN-taf, a pa DAN-nym at-DYE-la pra-DAZH, SRYED-nee CHEK pa-sta-YAN-na-va klee-YEN-ta pree-MYER-na vdvo-YE VY-she a-bych-na-va. vaz-ra-ZHEH-nee-ye a ras-KHO-dakh at-CHAS-tee SPRA-ved-lee-va: vee-CHYER-nya SMYE-na da-RA-zhe. ad-NA-ka ya nye na-kha-ZHOO da-ka-ZA-tyelstf a-VO, shto e-ka-NO-mee-ya pa-kry-VA-yet pa-TYE-ryu VY-rooch-kee. nap-RO-teev, ras-CHO-ty pa-KA-zy-va-yut a-BRAT-na-ye.) Read the structure. The claim is negative and stated first, which is the correct order for a written objection: a reader who disagrees should know immediately what is being opposed. С одной стороны concedes the objective size of the disputed category; с другой стороны immediately reframes it with именно, which concentrates the dispute on one element rather than on the volume of requests. The objection is conceded again with the same отчасти, and then answered in a way that is stronger than denial: я не нахожу доказательств того, что... — note the genitive after не нахожу, which denies the existence of an indefinite thing rather than attacking a specific claim. Напротив marks the reversal and the final sentence points to the writer's own numbers, which must exist for the sentence to be legitimate; if they do not, the sentence is a bluff, and the same framework that makes the argument readable also makes the bluff easy to locate.
depth.mistake: Four errors dominate learner arguments in Russian. (1) Claim substitution: the writer states a fact or a preference ('the evening shift is expensive') instead of a proposition that could be accepted or refused, and then wonders why no one agrees. (2) Warrant invisibility: the numbers are impeccable but the general principle that connects them to the conclusion is never stated, so a reader who rejects the principle reads the whole paragraph as irrelevant rather than wrong. (3) Concession inflation and deflation: either the writer invents a weak objection and defeats it, which a competent reader notices immediately, or the writer concedes so much that the claim disappears and the text becomes a summary of the topic. (4) Misused negation: using the genitive everywhere in order to sound indefinite, when a specific denial needs the accusative, or using the accusative everywhere and thereby claiming more than the writer can support. A fifth, Russian-specific error is the misuse of именно, which does not mean 'only' or 'even'; it points at the element that matters and should attach to a single word or phrase, not to a whole clause. Diagnostic procedure: mark your paragraph with four letters — C for claim, R for reason, W for warrant, O for objection and reply — and read it aloud. If any letter is missing, the paragraph is a summary; if two Cs appear with different content, you have two arguments and should write two paragraphs.
depth.application: Nonblocking task. Write a Russian argument of 120-160 words on a real question from your own work or study, using the four-slot structure. Requirements: one claim in the first two lines; at least one quantitative reason with its unit and its base, in the form taught in lesson 94; one warrant stated explicitly in a sentence of its own; one objection in the strongest form you can honestly state, with a reply; and one if-by sentence committing you to a falsifiable condition. Finish with a review date rather than a general assertion of benefit. Model response structure, applied to a different topic: claim — propose moving the weekly meeting to Wednesday; reason — attendance on Mondays was 60 percent of invitees across the last eight weeks, against 85 percent in the trial Wednesdays, both figures taken from the calendar records, not estimated; warrant — the meeting's value is realised only when the decision-makers are present; objection — Wednesday is a heavy delivery day for two teams, отчасти справедливо; reply — those two teams suggested a Wednesday slot in the calendar survey; if-by — если бы это касалось половины отдела, я бы не предлагал перенос; conclusion — перенести встречу на среду и вернуться к вопросу через месяц. Self-review rubric, seven points, one each: (1) the claim can be denied in one sentence by a reader; (2) every number carries its unit and its base; (3) the warrant is written out and is not a restatement of the claim; (4) the objection is one a real opponent would raise; (5) the reply answers the objection as stated, not a weaker version; (6) the if-by sentence names a condition under which you would withdraw; (7) a review date or mechanism is given. This is a composition exercise with a checklist. It does not verify that your claim is right, and the presence of a well-formed argument in Russian is evidence about your writing, not evidence about the merits of the decision.
depth.summary: An argument is a claim plus a reason plus a warrant plus an answered objection, and in Russian the four slots are marked by a small, learnable inventory: довод, возражение, возразить, согласиться, отчасти, напротив, именно, в целом, подтверждать and опровергать for the evidence verbs, and таким образом for the conclusion. The two grammatical resources that give Russian argument writing its precision are the conditional pair (если for a real condition, если бы plus the past for a hypothetical or counter-factual one) and the genitive of negation, which denies the existence of something indefinite. The limits are as important as the devices: reasons are not warrants, rates without bases do not decide anything, and an argument that cannot say what would change the writer's mind is a preference. The last two lessons turn to a different kind of writing — comparing options and recommending one, and then presenting the whole result in two registers — where the same four slots have to be filled in different grammar.

visual.title: Four-slot argument scaffold with concession branch
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: a left column of four slots (claim, reason plus warrant, objection plus reply, conclusion) and a right-hand branch for the if-by sentence that commits the writer to a falsifiable condition. Rendered as text steps, not as video or animation.
steps: Step 1 — Write the claim as one sentence a reader could deny. Output: a claim with no hedge that protects it from being wrong, plus a note on what would follow if it were rejected.
Step 2 — Add the reason with its unit and base, then write the warrant in a separate sentence. Output: two sentences, one factual, one principled, with the warrant visible rather than implied.

Step 3 — Fill the objection slot with the strongest honest counter-argument you can state, and label it with отчасти, напротив or в целом according to how much you concede. Output: an objection in the opponent's words, not a caricature.

Step 4 — Write the reply, answering the objection as stated, and mark whether you are confirming, failing to confirm, or refuting: подтверждать and опровергать are not interchangeable. Output: a reply with its evidential status labelled.

Step 5 — Add the if-by commitment and the review date, then read the whole paragraph aloud. Output: a text in which every one of the four slots can be pointed to by a stranger, which is the only test this lesson asks you to run.
