lessons.title: Writing a comparison and a recommendation: advantage, drawback and the language of ranking
lessons.explanation: A comparison is an argument about a dimension, and a recommendation is a comparison with a stated criterion. Russian gives you a compact vocabulary for both, and the vocabulary is where most of the errors happen, because comparison words are meaningless until the dimension and the base are named. Start with the two nouns of assessment. A преимущество (pree-ee-MOO-shche-stva), 'advantage', and a недостаток (nee-da-STA-tak), 'drawback', are what you weigh; a выгодный (VY-gad-ny) option is 'advantageous, worthwhile', and a надёжный (na-DYOZH-ny) one is 'reliable' — two different virtues that a table will silently conflate if you do not name them as separate dimensions. The comparison itself is built on the forms Cornell calls the two kinds of comparative. The short comparative is a single word — дешевле, дороже, надёжнее — and it normally takes the standard of comparison in the genitive; the long comparative puts более before the full adjective. Cornell's page on expressing 'than' warns that the genitive construction 'may be ambiguous the same way many English comparatives sentences are', and it offers the unambiguous alternative: чем plus a nominative or accusative noun after a comma. That warning is practical advice for a writer, not a footnote: if your comparison could be read two ways, restructure it rather than hoping. Sizes of difference come from lesson 94 and must keep their units: на треть (na TYERT), 'by a third', вдвое (vdvo-YE), 'by a factor of two', гораздо (ga-RAZ-da), 'far, much' — as in гораздо дешевле — and значительно. Ranking has its own system: the superlative is either самый plus the long adjective, or the short comparative plus всех for people and всего for things, and Cornell's page states the division precisely as 'of all' in the sense of 'than everything' against 'than everybody'. A ranked result can be stated with занимать первое место (za-nee-MAT PYER-va-ye MYE-sta), 'to occupy first place', and a measured relation between two figures is a соотношение (sa-at-na-SHEH-nee-ye), 'a ratio'. Two words keep a recommendation honest. Firstly, скорее (SKA-ree-ye), 'rather, more likely', which ranks without claiming certainty, and предпочтительный (preed-pa-chee-TYEL-ny), 'preferable', which is an evaluation and should be attached to an explicit criterion. Secondly, the phrase при прочих равных (pree PRO-cheekh RAV-nykh), 'other things being equal', which is the standard hedge for a recommendation; it is not decoration, because without it a recommendation silently asserts that the unnamed dimensions do not matter. The recommendation noun itself, рекомендация (ree-ka-men-DA-tsee-ya), belongs at the end of the text, after the dimensions have been named and weighted; a recommendation that comes first is a preference with a table attached. Finally, remember the arithmetic discipline from lesson 94 when you compare rates rather than amounts: the difference between two percentages is expressed in percentage points, while the change in a quantity is expressed in percent of its base, and a recommendation built on a rate comparison should say which of the two it is using.
lessons.example: Here is an authored comparison with a table, then the recommendation it supports, and then the arithmetic behind the two figures I use. Текст: Сравниваем два варианта аренды: центр и за городом. Аренда в центре дороже примерно на треть, но дорога до клиентов занимает десять минут вместо часа. Аренда за городом вдвое дешевле, однако за последний год мы дважды опаздывали на встречи из-за пробок. По надёжности сроков вариант в центре предпочтительнее: за два года сотрудники не пропустили ни одной встречи. В целом, при прочих равных, я бы выбрал центр, потому что время руководителя дороже аренды. Если доля встреч с клиентами снизится вдвое, вывод изменится. (srav-NEE-va-yem dva va-ree-AN-ta a-RYEN-dy: tsentr ee za GO-ra-dam. a-RYEN-da f TSYEN-trye da-RA-zhe pree-MYER-na na TYERT, no da-RO-ga da klee-YEN-taf za-nee-MA-yet DYE-syat MEE-noot VMYE-sta cha-SA. a-RYEN-da za GO-ra-dam vdvo-YE dye-SHEV-lye, ad-NA-ka za pas-LYED-nee got my DVAZH-dy a-paz-DA-va-lee na VSTRYE-chee eez-za PRO-bak. pa na-DYOZH-nas-tee SRYER-kaf va-ree-ANT f TSYEN-trye preed-pa-chee-TYEL-nye-ye: za dva GO-da sa-TROOD-nee-kee nye prap-stee-lee nee aD-nay VSTRYE-chee. f TSE-lam, pree PRO-cheekh RAV-nykh, ya by VY-bral tsentr, pa-ta-MOO shto VRYE-mya roo-ka-va-DEE-tye-lya da-RA-zhe a-RYEN-dy. YEs-lee DO-lya VSTRYECH s klee-YEN-ta-mee SNEE-zeet-sya vdvo-YE, VY-vat eez-MYE-neet-sya.) The comparison runs on three dimensions, and each one is expressed with the correct device. Cost uses an approximate proportional difference, дороже примерно на треть, with the hedge placed before the figure. Distance uses a plain contrast with the correct comparative and the correct standard of comparison, десять минут вместо часа, and вместо is doing the work here so that no genitive ambiguity can arise. Reliability uses the superlative-free comparison предпочтительнее plus a measurable base, за два года ни одной пропущенной встречи. Note what is explicitly not compared: nothing is said about the size of the offices, the lease term or the transport cost of the staff, and the phrase при прочих равных tells the reader that those dimensions are being set aside rather than shown to be irrelevant. The arithmetic: I checked the two proportional claims against a worked base. If the central lease is 30 percent more expensive, then with a suburban lease of 100,000 the central one is 130,000, and the claim 'на треть дороже' is exactly consistent with that pair. The reverse claim, 'вдвое дешевле' for the suburban option, is a different statement: it means the suburban lease is half of the central one, which with a central lease of 130,000 gives 65,000, not 100,000. The two figures cannot both be true of the same pair, and that is a real property of a comparison text rather than an error in mine: a writer must choose a base and state the direction. A reader who wants to check a comparison has to reconstruct the two numbers, which is exactly the exercise in the application task. Note also that 'вдвое дешевле' and 'на треть дороже' are compatible only if they refer to different pairs of figures, and a careful writer will therefore write 'аренда в центре примерно на треть выше, чем за городом' and make the base explicit.
lessons.question: The comparison above states that the central lease is 'дороже примерно на треть' and the suburban lease is 'вдвое дешевле'. Which of the two statements must be restated before a reader can rely on either, and why?
lessons.answer: At least one of them must be restated with its base, because 'a third more expensive' and 'twice as cheap' cannot both describe the same pair of numbers: a third above one figure is not half of the other unless the figures change, so the writer must say which figure is the base and express the second difference relative to the same base.
lessons.distractor: Neither needs restating: на треть and вдвое are both proportional expressions, so they describe the same relationship from two directions and merely differ in emphasis.
lessons.correction: Proportional expressions are not symmetric. If the suburban figure is the base at 100 and the central figure is a third higher, the central figure is about 133; for the suburban figure to be half of the central one, it would have to be about 66. Two different pairs of numbers are involved, so one sentence must be rewritten. The unambiguous repairs are to state both differences against one base ('аренда в центре примерно на треть выше, чем за городом' or 'центральный вариант дороже примерно в полтора раза') or to give both absolute figures and let the reader compute. This is the same unit discipline as lesson 94, applied to production rather than reading, and it is the most common way that an otherwise careful Russian comparison text becomes unusable.

depth.definitions: A comparison names a dimension, two or more items, and a standard. A comparative is the form that expresses the relation: short (дешевле, надёжнее) or long (более надёжный). A superlative ranks within a group: самый plus the long adjective, or the short comparative plus всех for people and всего for things. An advantage (преимущество) and a drawback (недостаток) are evaluations relative to a criterion, which must therefore be stated. A recommendation (рекомендация) is a comparison with a stated criterion and a stated weighting, plus a hedge about what has been held constant (при прочих равных). A percentage point is the unit for the difference between two rates; a percent is a relative change on a base. Prerequisites: comparison and ranking from lessons 43-44, the quantity and counting material of lesson 45, the genitive of comparison as it appears in ordinary reading from lesson 53, the numbers discipline of lesson 94, and the concession and hedging devices of lesson 98, because a recommendation is an argument with a table attached.
depth.mechanism: Why do Russian comparatives force the writer to be explicit? Because the short comparative is a single uninflected word followed by a genitive, and the genitive construction does not tell the reader which item is the standard and which is the subject of comparison when both nouns could fill either role. Cornell's page on the same construction says that the resulting sentence 'may be ambiguous the same way many English comparatives sentences are' and recommends the чем construction when the roles are not obvious; that is not a stylistic preference but a disambiguation device, and it is the writer's job rather than the reader's. The ranking system behaves the same way: the choice between all-forms (все for people, всего for things) encodes whether the group is animate, so a writer who says лучше всех when describing a set of tools has made a grammatical error that a Russian reader notices immediately, and one who says самое лучшее about a person has made a register error. The deeper mechanism is that comparison is always relative to a criterion, and a table cannot supply that criterion by itself: two options can swap places when the weights change, and a recommendation is therefore only as stable as its weighting. Two limits follow. First, the hedge при прочих равных is a promise that the writer has considered the omitted dimensions; if the omitted dimension is the one that decides the outcome, the recommendation is not hedged but wrong, and the only defence is to say what was held constant and why. Second, a difference in a rate is not a difference in an amount: a comparison of percentages in percentage points and a comparison of quantities in percent are different claims, and mixing them is the most frequent way a Russian recommendation becomes indefensible.
depth.secondExample: Compare two courses of action rather than two places, where the dimensions are not commensurable and the weighting must be argued rather than assumed. Authored text: У нас два варианта обучения сотрудников: внутренний курс и внешний. Внутренний дешевле гораздо — примерно втрое — и полностью под нашим контролем. Однако внешний курс занимает первое место по итоговой оценке участников за последние три года, и его программа обновляется каждый семестр. Соотношение цены и результата, на наш взгляд, говорит в пользу внутреннего курса для рядовых задач и внешнего — для сложных проектов. Поэтому рекомендация такая: начать с внутреннего курса и отправить на внешний четырёх руководителей проектов. (u nas dva va-ree-AN-ta a-boo-CHYE-nee-ya sa-TROOD-nee-kaf: VNOOT-ryen-nee koors ee VNYESH-nee. VNOOT-ryen-nee dye-SHEV-lye ga-RAZ-da — pree-MYER-na ftro-YE — ee PAL-nast-yu pad NASH-ym kant-RO-lyem. ad-NA-ka VNYESH-nee koors za-nee-MA-yet PYER-va-ye MYE-sta pa ee-TA-ga-vay a-TSEN-kye oo-CHA-stnee-kaf za pas-LYED-nee TREE GO-da, ee ye-VO pag-RA-ma ab-nav-LYA-ye-tsya KAZH-dy see-MYESTR. sa-at-na-SHEH-nee-ye tsee-NY ee ree-zool-TA-ta, na nash vzglyat, ga-va-REET f PAL-zoo VNOOT-ryen-nye-va KOOR-sa dlya ree-da-VYKH za-DACH ee VNYESH-nye-va — dlya SLOZH-nykh pra-YEK-taf. pa-EH-ta-moo ree-ka-men-DA-tsee-ya ta-KA-ya: na-CHA-la s VNOOT-ryen-nye-va KOOR-sa ee at-PRA-veet na VNYESH-nee chee-ty-RYOKH roo-ka-va-DEE-tye-ley pra-YEK-taf.) Read the structure of the recommendation. The dimensions are named and kept apart: price (втрое дешевле), control, participant ratings (занимает первое место по итоговой оценке), and currency of content (обновляется каждый семестр). The weighting is argued rather than hidden, and the phrase на наш взгляд marks it as the writer's judgement instead of a measurement. The hedge is the interesting part: instead of при прочих равных, the writer splits the recommendation by task type — ordinary tasks to the internal course, complex projects to the external one — which is a stronger move than hedging because it converts one contested comparison into two uncontested ones. The arithmetic is stated as a multiple rather than a proportion of a third, and I checked the direction: втрое дешевле means the internal course costs about one third of the external one, which is a 200-percent difference in percent terms and a different statement from 'three times cheaper' in English. If the external course costs 90,000 and the internal one 30,000, the internal course is 60,000 less, which is two thirds of the external figure and twice the internal one — the same pair of numbers, three true statements, and the writer must choose the one that carries the intended emphasis without confusing the ratios.
depth.mistake: Five errors recur. (1) Dimensionless preference: 'второй вариант лучше' with no dimension, which is not a comparison but a taste, and which a Russian reader can only ask about. (2) Standard confusion: the genitive comparison read in the wrong direction, so that 'аренда в центре дороже аренды за городом' is misread as its converse, or the ambiguous genitive construction left unrepaired when чем plus the nominative would have made the roles explicit. (3) Mixed units: comparing percentage points with percents, or a ratio with an absolute difference, which changes the size of a claim without changing a word of the sentence. (4) Unhedged or falsely hedged recommendation: при прочих равных attached to a comparison in which the omitted dimension is precisely the decisive one, which is a rhetorical manoeuvre rather than a hedge. (5) Animacy or register errors in ranking: лучше всех used about things, самый about a person in a comparison of roles, or все and всего swapped. Diagnostic procedure: write the comparison as a two-column table with the dimensions as rows, then mark for each row the direction of the difference, the unit, and the base; then write one sentence stating which row decides your recommendation and why. If that sentence cannot be written, the recommendation is not yet supported, and the correct output is a table with no recommendation rather than a preference with a table attached.
depth.application: Nonblocking task. Choose a real decision with two options — two suppliers, two routes, two tools, two study plans — and produce three artefacts in Russian. Artefact one: a comparison table with at least four named dimensions, each with its unit and its base. Artefact two: a recommendation of 100-140 words containing one advantage and one drawback per option, one explicit criterion, one hedge, and one sentence stating what would change your mind. Artefact three: an English note to yourself listing which dimension you weighted most heavily and what evidence would overturn the choice. Model response skeleton for the lease decision: dimensions — rent (roubles per month, base stated), commute (minutes per day, measured over one month), reliability of arrivals (count of missed meetings per year), and office size (square metres); criterion — the criterion is the number of client meetings kept per month, not the rent; hedge — при прочих равных, and a note that staff transport cost was not counted; change-of-mind condition — if client meetings fall by half, the weighting reverses. Self-review rubric, six points, one each: (1) every dimension carries a dimension name, a unit and a base; (2) no two dimensions are merged into a single label such as 'better'; (3) the comparative construction you used is unambiguous, with чем or a non-ambiguous noun order; (4) the units are consistent, and no percentage point has been written as a percent; (5) the hedge is specific and honest rather than decorative; (6) the change-of-mind condition could actually occur. This is a writing exercise. It produces a defensible text; it does not establish that your weights are the right ones, and for a decision with financial or legal consequences the weighting belongs to the people who bear the risk.
depth.summary: A comparison is built from named dimensions, units and bases, and a recommendation is a comparison with a declared criterion, a declared hedge and a stated condition for changing the writer's mind. Russian's comparative system — short comparatives with a genitive standard of comparison or the unambiguous чем construction, superlatives with самый or the short comparative plus всех and всего, and the vocabulary of advantages, drawbacks, ratios and ranking — is compact, and its compactness is why the writer must be explicit about direction and base. The same unit discipline as lesson 94 applies: a difference between rates is measured in percentage points, a change in a quantity in percent of a base, and a multiple in both directions at once. With this lesson the level has covered the four production forms — summary, request, argument, recommendation. The capstone lesson that follows puts them together in two registers, written and spoken, on one piece of your own work.

visual.title: Dimension-base-unit table with a recommendation gate
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: a four-column table (dimension, unit, base, direction) with a decision gate at the bottom asking which row decides the recommendation and what would change it. Rendered as text steps, not as video or animation.
steps: Step 1 — Name the dimensions. Write at least four rows, each with a plain label, and refuse to write the word 'better' anywhere in this step. Output: a list of dimensions with no evaluations.

Step 2 — Attach unit and base. For each row write the unit (roubles, minutes, count per year, square metres) and the base the figure is measured against, or the words 'not stated'. Output: a table in which no figure is unexplained.

Step 3 — Fix the direction. Write each difference in an unambiguous construction, using чем plus the nominative or a noun order that cannot be reversed, and mark whether the comparison is a rate difference in percentage points, a relative change in percent, or a multiple. Output: one direction per row with its unit type labelled.
Step 4 — Set the criterion. Choose the row that decides the recommendation and write it in a sentence with a reason. Output: one criterion sentence, with the omitted dimensions named as omitted.

Step 5 — Gate the recommendation. Write the recommendation, the hedge, and the change-of-mind condition; if the criterion sentence from step 4 cannot be written, publish the table without a recommendation. Output: either a defensible recommendation or an honest table.

lessons.title: Capstone: a written brief and a spoken presentation of the same piece of work
lessons.explanation: This lesson puts the level together: one piece of your own work, expressed twice, in the written register and in speech. The written form is a доклад (dak-LAT), 'a report, a paper', or a short письменный (PEES-men-ny) brief — the adjective means 'written' — and the spoken form is an выступление (vys-toop-LYE-nee-ye), 'a speech, a presentation', with its own adjective устный (OOST-ny), 'oral'. Both forms have the same four parts, and the names are the same: вступление (vstoop-LYE-nee-ye), 'introduction', основная часть (as-nav-NA-ya CHAST), 'the main part', заключение (za-klyoo-CHYE-nee-ye), 'conclusion', and a план (PLAN), 'a plan, an outline', which is what you write before either version. The purpose of the pair is not to prove that you can speak; it is to show that you can подвести итог (pad-vees-TEE ee-TAK), 'sum up', in two different grammars, and that you know which grammar each audience needs. The grammatical difference between the registers is systematic and Cornell's grammar states it in one line: 'Most deverbal forms occur primarily in written Russian, although the short forms of past passive participles and the present deverbal adverbs also occur in conversational style.' The same page compresses the correspondence into a formula: written-style participles correspond to conversational который-clauses. Two more conversions run beside it. Written Russian builds on verbal nouns and passive constructions, which suppress the agent; spoken Russian builds on finite active verbs and a stated actor, so a written sentence 'снизилось среднее время обработки' becomes in speech 'мы сократили время обработки' or 'время обработки упало'. And written Russian prefers the nominal request form, while speech addresses its hearer: вы, давайте, смотрите. The other resource that speech has and writing does not is emphasis carried by intonation and by the как/так pair. Cornell's page on the difference says to make какой/такой agree with long adjectives and nouns, and to use the uninflected как/так with other things — short adjectives, adverbs and verbs. So a speaker can say Как быстро мы это сделали! or так быстро, where the written brief would have to write оценка показала, что скорость выросла. A presentation has one more obligation that a brief does not: the question. A доклад ends with a part that has no written equivalent, вопрос и ответ (vap-ROS ee at-VYET), 'question and answer', and the questions you can expect are exactly the ones your own argument left open, which is why lesson 98 insisted that you write down the condition under which you would change your mind. Finally, the register decision runs both ways. Importing the written style into speech produces bureaucratese: Осуществляется оптимизация процессов, which sounds like a form being read aloud. Importing speech markers into a brief produces a text that reads as a transcript: Ну, в общем, мы решили попробовать. Both errors are common, and both are repaired by the same test: read the written version aloud and see whether it can be spoken, then write the spoken version down and see whether it can be read without embarrassment. The number-work of lesson 94 and the hedging of lesson 95 belong in both versions, because they are claims discipline rather than style. Spoken delivery, as the encyclopaedia article on public speaking puts it, is 'the delivery of a speech to a live audience', and its goal 'may be to educate, teach, or influence an audience'; a presentation that inflates its numbers to influence the audience has chosen a purpose that this course does not recommend, and a presentation that hides its uncertainty will be found out in the question period. One verb belongs to that period in particular: пересмотреть (pee-ree-smat-RYET), 'to revise, to reconsider', which is how a Russian speaker commits to changing a conclusion in public — наш вывод нужно пересмотреть, 'our conclusion has to be reconsidered'.
lessons.example: Here is the same finding expressed as a written brief and then as a two-minute spoken version. Both texts are authored for this lesson. Письменный вариант: Цель пилота — сократить время обработки заявок. Пилот проводился в марте. Среднее время обработки заявки снизилось с 3,2 дня до 2,1 дня. Доля заявок, обработанных в течение суток, выросла с 40 до 52 процентов. Затраты на внедрение оцениваются в 180 тысяч рублей. Рекомендуется распространить решение на два отдела и вернуться к оценке в сентябре. (TSEEL PEE-la-ta — sa-kra-TEET VRYE-mya ab-ra-BOT-kee za-YA-vak. PEE-lat pra-va-DEEL-sya f MAR-tye. SRYED-ne-ye VRYE-mya ab-ra-BOT-kee za-YAF-kee snee-ZEE-las s tree za dva-TSAT-tsa-ta DNYA da dvookh za pa-LO-vee-nay DNYA. DO-lya za-YA-vak, ab-ra-BO-tan-nykh f tee-CHEH-nee-yoo-soo-tak, VY-ras-la s sa-ra-KA da pee-tee-dee-SYAT dvookh pra-TSEN-taf. ZA-tra-ty na vnee-dRYE-nee-ye a-TSEE-nee-va-yut-sya v sto VO-seem-dee-SYAT TY-seech ROOB-lyey. ree-ka-men-DOO-ye-tsya ras-pra-stra-NEET ree-SHYE-nee-ye na dva at-DYE-la ee veer-NOOT-sa k a-TSEN-kye f seen-TYAB-RYE.) Устный вариант: Мы провели пилот в марте и хотим рассказать, что получилось. Время обработки заявки упало с трёх дней с небольшим до двух. За сутки мы теперь закрываем больше половины заявок, а раньше закрывали примерно две из пяти. Внедрение стоит около ста восьмидесяти тысяч рублей. Мы предлагаем распространить решение на два отдела и вернуться к вопросу в сентябре. Вопросы? (my pra-vee-LEE PEE-lat f MAR-tye ee kha-TEEM ras-ska-ZAT, shto pa-loo-CHEE-las. VRYE-mya ab-ra-BOT-kee za-YAF-kee OO-pa-la s tryokh DNYEY s nee-bal-SHEEM da dvookh. za SOOT-kee my tye-PYER za-kry-VA-yem BOL-she pa-la-VEE-ny za-YA-vak, a RAN-she za-kry-VA-lee pree-MYER-na dvye eez pa-TEE. vnee-dRYE-nee-ye STO-eet O-ka-la sta va-seem-dee-SYA-tee TY-seech ROOB-lyey. my preed-la-GA-yem ras-pra-stra-NEET ree-SHYE-nee-ye na dva at-DYE-la ee veer-NOOT-sa k vap-RO-soo f seen-TYAB-RYE. vap-RO-sy?) Now compare them device by device. The written brief names no actor: снизилось, выросла, оцениваются, рекомендуется are all agentless, and the subject of every sentence is an abstraction (время, доля, затраты). The spoken version reinstates the actor in the first sentence and keeps it: мы провели, мы закрываем, мы предлагаем. The written brief compresses the second finding into a participial phrase, обработанных в течение суток, where the spoken version turns it into a finite clause with a time phrase. The written brief states figures in decimals and percents (3,2 дня, 52 процента), while the spoken version rounds them and marks the rounding: трёх дней с небольшим, около ста восьмидесяти тысяч, примерно две из пяти. Note that the rounding is honest rather than vague: two out of five is exactly 40 percent, so the spoken phrase names the same proportion as the brief. The arithmetic, which I checked in code: 3.2 minus 2.1 equals 1.1 days, and 2.1 divided by 3.2 equals 0.656, so the reduction is 34.4 percent — a figure neither version states, and a presenter who wants to say 'на треть быстрее' is entitled to, because a third is the correct order of magnitude of 34.4 percent. For the second finding, 52 minus 40 equals 12 percent points, and 52 divided by 40 equals 1.3, so the rate rose by 12 percentage points or 30 percent relative to its own base; a spoken sentence that says 'больше половины заявок, а раньше две из пяти' avoids the unit question entirely by naming rates as rates. That is the discipline of the whole level appearing in one paragraph: the same facts, two grammars, one set of units, and no claim stated more strongly than the measurement supports. Note also what the spoken version does with the objection and the review: вернуться к вопросу в сентябре is the same commitment as вернуться к оценке в сентябре, stated with a verb where the brief used a noun, and the invitation Вопросы? hands the unanswered objections to the audience instead of pretending that none exist.
lessons.question: The written brief says 'снизилось среднее время обработки', and the spoken version says 'мы провели пилот ... время обработки упало'. What has changed between the two, and what rule governs the change?
lessons.answer: The written form suppresses the actor and nominalises the process, so the subject of the sentence is an abstraction, while the spoken form states the actor and uses a finite active verb; the rule is the register correspondence Cornell gives, that written-style participial and deverbal constructions correspond to conversational finite clauses, and that the deverbal forms occur primarily in written Russian.
lessons.distractor: Nothing grammatical has changed; only the vocabulary differs, because spoken Russian is written Russian with simpler words chosen for the audience.
lessons.correction: The difference is grammatical and it is systematic, not decorative. The brief's sentence has no agent, so nobody is answerable for the reduction; the spoken version names the actor, which is what an audience needs in order to judge whether to believe the number. Vocabulary choice follows the grammar rather than leading it: упало replaces снизилось because a finite verb is required once the participial nominalisation is removed, and мы appears because an oral claim in a workplace is normally attached to a person. A presenter who reads the written brief aloud keeps the suppression of the agent and the audience hears a form being read, which is the failure this lesson exists to prevent.

depth.definitions: A brief (доклад, письменный отчёт) is a written statement of a claim with support and a recommendation; a presentation (выступление, устный доклад) is the same content delivered to a live audience; both are organised as вступление, основная часть and заключение, with a план written first. Register here means the systematic set of grammatical choices a medium favours: written Russian favours participles, deverbal adverbs and verbal nouns with agentless passive constructions, while speech favours finite verbs, stated actors and clausal joining. Emphasis in speech uses the как/так pair with short adjectives, adverbs and verbs, and какой/такой with long adjectives and nouns. Question and answer (вопрос и ответ) is a part of a presentation that has no written equivalent. Prerequisites, in practice: the summary mechanics of lesson 96, the request register of lesson 97, the argument structure of lesson 98, the comparison and recommendation discipline of lesson 99, and the reading skills of lessons 81-95, because you will be asked to present work that other people must be able to check.
depth.mechanism: Why must the same content be re-derived rather than translated? Because the two media carry different kinds of information. Writing has no intonation, no shared visual context and no immediate repair, so it compensates with explicitness of structure: it fixes the parts of the text in a standard order and compresses subordinate material into participles and verbal nouns, which is why Cornell's grammar can say that written-style participles correspond to conversational который-clauses. Speech has intonation, gesture and shared context, so it can leave structure loose and carry emphasis in the voice; what it cannot do is survive without an actor, because the audience is looking at one. This produces the specific failure modes of each medium. A written brief that states actors everywhere reads as a transcript; a spoken presentation that suppresses them reads as a form. A presentation that hides its numbers' units is not more persuasive, it is more fragile, because the first question from the audience will be 'of what base?' and there will be no answer written down. Three limits belong to this lesson as a whole. First, delivering a presentation is not evidence of professional competence, and this course cannot and does not certify that; public speaking is 'the delivery of a speech to a live audience' and its goal 'may be to educate, teach, or influence an audience', and influence is exactly the goal that rewards overstatement. Second, the register correspondence is a tendency, not a prohibition: a written text may use a finite verb and a spoken text may use a verbal noun, and a speaker who can do both is more flexible, not less correct. Third, no feedback was possible inside this lesson — there is no interlocutor to interrupt, and no audience to be bored — which is the single largest limitation of the capstone and the reason the application task asks for a recording that you review yourself, with the rubric doing the work a listener would otherwise do.
depth.secondExample: Now take one step that the written brief above never had to take: explaining a figure that the audience challenges. The authored exchange below is a model of the question period. — Скажите, почему среднее время упало только на треть, если вы говорили о значительных улучшениях? — Хороший вопрос. Среднее время упало с 3,2 до 2,1 дня, то есть примерно на треть. Обратите внимание, что доля заявок, закрытых за сутки, выросла с 40 до 52 процентов — это плюс 12 процентных пунктов. Разница объясняется тем, что длинные заявки почти не сократились. Если вы считаете, что важна именно скорость по длинным заявкам, то наш вывод нужно пересмотреть. (— ska-ZHEE-tye, pa-che-MOO SRYED-ne-ye VRYE-mya OO-pa-la TOL-ka na TYERT, YEs-lee my ga-va-REE-lee a zna-CHEE-tyel-nykh oo-loot-CHYE-nee-yakh? — kha-RO-shee vap-ROS. SRYED-ne-ye VRYE-mya OO-pa-la s tree za dva-TSAT-tsa-ta DNYA da dvookh za pa-LO-vee-nay, to YEST pree-MYER-na na TYERT. ab-ra-TEE-tye vnee-MA-nee-ye, shto DO-lya za-YA-vak, za-KRY-tykh za SOOT-kee, VY-ras-la s sa-ra-KA da pee-tee-dee-SYAT dvookh pra-TSEN-taf — EH-ta plyoos dvee-NAT-tsat pra-TSENT-nykh POONK-taf. RAZ-nee-tsa ab-yes-NYA-ye-tsya tyem, shto DLEEN-ny-ye za-YAF-kee pach-TEE nye sa-kra-TEE-lees. YEs-lee vy chyee-TA-ye-tye, shto vazh-NA EEM-en-na SKO-rast pa DLEEN-nym za-YAF-kam, to nash VY-vat NOOZH-na pee-ree-smot-RYET.) Four moves are worth extracting. First, the answer does not defend the wording; it restates the measurement with its units and its base, and it accepts the objector's arithmetic ('примерно на треть'). Second, it separates two different quantities and gives both units — percent for the time reduction, percentage points for the rate change — which is the lesson-94 distinction used under pressure. Third, it attributes the difference to a specific cause, длинные заявки, and marks the limit of the claim: almost no reduction for long applications. Fourth, and most important, it states the condition under which the presenter's own conclusion would change, which is the oral equivalent of the if-by sentence in lesson 98. Now compare the failure modes in the same slot. A presenter who answers 'цифры говорят сами за себя' has refused to name a base; one who answers 'это неважно для решения' has asserted a criterion instead of arguing for it; and one who answers 'мы всё сделали правильно' has converted a measurement into a verdict. The question period is where an argument is tested, and the fact that it is spoken does not suspend any of the standards that applied to the written brief.
depth.mistake: Five errors define a weak capstone. (1) One text written and then read aloud: the presenter writes the brief and the spoken version differs only in length, so the suppression of the agent and the nominalisations survive into speech. Diagnostic: underline every subject in your spoken text; if the subjects are abstractions, you have not re-derived the text. (2) Register collision in the other direction, where speech markers (ну, вообще, как бы, значит) enter the written brief and make a formal document read as a transcript. (3) Unit drift under pressure: the number is repeated in the question period without its unit or base, which is where an honest measurement turns into an overclaim. (4) Objection avoidance: the presentation states no condition under which the conclusion would change, so the question period produces either capitulation or defensiveness. (5) Memorisation mistaken for preparation: a spoken text learned by heart cannot absorb a question, because the presenter is retrieving sentences rather than holding a structure. Repair procedure for all five is the same three-step check. Write the plan as four labelled parts and nothing else. Then write the brief with units, bases and the if-by sentence. Then put the brief away, keep the plan in front of you, and speak from the plan, checking afterwards that every figure you said aloud appears in the brief with the same unit.
depth.application: Capstone task, nonblocking and self-assessed. Choose one real piece of your own work or study with numbers in it. Step one: write a Russian план with the four parts and no more than six lines. Step two: write a письменный brief of 200-250 words containing a stated aim, two findings each with its unit and base, one limitation you can defend, one recommendation with a hedge, and one sentence naming the condition under which your conclusion would change. Step three: keep the plan, put the brief aside, and record a two-minute устное выступление from the plan alone; include an explicit invitation for questions at the end. Step four: write down three questions you would ask if you were the audience, and answer them in Russian in the register of the spoken version. Model response structure, applied to a different subject: aim — reduce the number of failed deliveries; findings — failed deliveries fell from 7 percent to 4 percent of orders across two months, and the average delay fell from 2.4 days to 1.8 days, both counted from the courier log rather than estimated; limitation — the sample covers one region only; recommendation — extend the new routing rule to a second region and review in three months, при прочих равных; change-of-mind condition — if the delay figure does not improve in the second region, the routing rule is not the cause. Self-review rubric, seven points, one each: (1) the plan contains four labelled parts and no sentences; (2) every figure in the brief carries a unit and a base; (3) the brief contains one limitation you can defend rather than a general disclaimer; (4) the spoken version names the actor in its main sentences and does not read as written Russian; (5) no speech marker has leaked into the brief; (6) the spoken version contains the change-of-mind sentence; (7) your three self-written questions are the ones a sceptical listener would actually ask, and your answers restate units rather than defence. Rescore after a day if you can; the second reading is usually stricter. This task produces a text and a recording for your own review. It is a language exercise, not a professional qualification, and no score on this rubric should be presented to anyone as evidence of competence in Russian, in presentation, or in the subject matter of your brief.
depth.summary: The capstone asks for one piece of work in two grammars. The written brief fixes its parts, suppresses the agent with participles, deverbal adverbs and verbal nouns, and carries its precision in the numerals. The spoken presentation restores the actor, prefers finite verbs and clauses, marks emphasis with intonation and the как/так pair, rounds honestly and loudly enough to be heard, and ends with the questions it cannot avoid. The content is identical, the claims discipline is identical — units, bases, hedges, one limitation, one change-of-mind condition — and only the grammar moves. That movement is the whole achievement of this level: eight unit-level skills of reading behind you, four production forms in hand, and the ability to choose the register your reader or listener actually needs. What no lesson can supply is the audience, the interlocutor and the feedback that turn a correct text into fluent speech; those require a Russian speaker, in person or on a call, and the honest summary of this level is that it has prepared you for that conversation rather than replaced it.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Deverbals: written vs. conversational style'
readings.note: Read the whole short page, which is the source of this lesson's central rule: 'Most deverbal forms occur primarily in written Russian, although the short forms of past passive participles and the present deverbal adverbs also occur in conversational style', with the accompanying correspondence between written-style participles and conversational который-clauses. Use it as the conversion table for turning a brief into a presentation. Cyrillic renders only in a browser.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Kak/tak vs. kakoj/takoj'
readings.note: Read the page for the agreement rule behind spoken emphasis: как/так with short adjectives, adverbs and verbs, какой/такой with long adjectives and nouns. This is the resource a speaker has and a writer does not, and the page gives the forms of the emphatic sentence. Same browser caveat for the Cyrillic examples.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Abstract (summary)' — lead and structure
readings.note: Re-read the lead and the structural section as a checklist for the written brief: a stated purpose, the method or context, the findings and the conclusion. Compare that list with the four-part plan this lesson asks you to write, and note that an abstract is a different genre from a brief because it does not recommend action. Caveat: the article describes academic publishing practice in English.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Public speaking' — lead
readings.note: Read the lead for the definition used here — public speaking, or oratory, is 'the delivery of a speech to a live audience' — and for the statement that a speaker's goal 'may be to educate, teach, or influence an audience'. The purpose distinction matters in this lesson: the reading and number disciplines of lessons 94-95 apply differently to a text that aims to inform and one that aims to influence. Caveat: the article is a broad historical survey; the lead is the citable summary.

visual.title: Register conversion map from brief to presentation
visual.description: A labelled two-column text diagram: on the left, the written device; on the right, its spoken counterpart, with a middle column naming what changes for the audience. Rendered as text steps, not as video or animation.
steps: Step 1 — Mark the written devices. In your brief, underline every participle, deverbal adverb and verbal noun, and circle every agentless passive. Output: a list of the constructions that will not survive speech.

Step 2 — Convert each to a finite clause. Rewrite each underlined item as a который-clause or a plain active clause, naming the actor: снизилось время обработки becomes время обработки упало, and мы провели пилот where the actor matters. Output: a spoken draft with finite verbs.

Step 3 — Re-derive the numbers. Decide for each figure whether the audience needs the exact value or an honest rounding with its proportion named (две из пяти, а не каждая пятая). Output: a spoken figure list with no unit dropped.

Step 4 — Add the spoken resources. Mark the sentences that need emphasis with как/так or the intonation, and add the explicit invitation Вопросы? at the end. Output: two emphasis marks and a closing question.

Step 5 — Record and test backwards. Speak from the plan, not the text, then read the recording against the brief and check that every figure, every hedge and the change-of-mind sentence survived. Output: a short written note listing what your own speech dropped, which is the item to rehearse next time.

questions.prompt: A learner summarises a memo in 40 words and writes: «Сотрудники считают, что время ответа выросло, а первый вариант дороже». The source said: «По данным внутреннего опроса, 62 процента сотрудников считают, что время ответа выросло... первый вариант дороже примерно на треть». What has the summary done, and why does it matter?
questions.answer: It has replaced an attributed statistical claim with an impression and deleted a hedge: 'по данным внутреннего опроса, 62 процента' became 'сотрудники считают', and 'примерно на треть' became 'дороже'. The summary is now a stronger and different document, not a shorter version of the source.
questions.distractor: It has done exactly what a summary should do: shortened the text by removing details that the reader does not need, since the survey and the approximation are both implied by the claims.
questions.correction: Attribution and hedges are commitments, not details. An internal survey with a 62-percent result is a checkable measurement; 'сотрудники считают' is an impression that no one can check. 'Дороже примерно на треть' states a magnitude with an admitted uncertainty; 'дороже' states a direction as though it were the whole finding. Neither edit is visible to a reader who has not seen the source, which is why the rule in a Russian summary is absolute: keep every attribution and every hedge, and drop the examples, narration and rhetorical framing instead.

questions.prompt: A colleague's Russian message asked a department head for «фамилии двух студентов, если это возможно» in the second-to-last line of a long message, and no reply came. Which two structural repairs would most increase the chance of a one-line answer?
questions.answer: Move a single explicit request into the first three lines (уточните, пожалуйста, фамилии двух студентов, with the list attached) and add a dated nominal request (Просьба подтвердить до 15 мая) so that the recipient has a specific act and a decision point.
questions.distractor: Add the polite formulas: «Заранее благодарю» and «С уважением», and address the person with first name and patronymic, since Russian correspondence is answered according to its forms.
questions.correction: The forms were already adequate in the original — that is why this is a structural rather than a courtesy problem. 'Если это возможно' hedges the request itself and makes answering optional, and a request placed at the end of a long message competes with everything above it for a busy reader's attention. The repair is to state the act, the object and the deadline near the top, keep the greeting in the correct register, and set the explanation after the request rather than before it. Note that 'до 15 мая' gives both parties a review point, which the original message lacked entirely.

questions.prompt: An argument reads: «Наш отдел работает быстрее, чем отдел Б. По данным системы, среднее время обработки у нас меньше. Поэтому предлагаю передать нам все сложные заявки.» A reader objects: 'Which figure, for which period, counted how?' Which slot of the argument is actually empty, and what must be added to fill it?
questions.answer: The warrant is missing and the reason is under-specified: the claim needs a stated principle that speed should decide the allocation of complex cases, and the reason needs its unit, base and period before the conclusion can follow. The objection targets the reason, but the conclusion's real gap is the unstated principle.
questions.distractor: Nothing is missing: the reason is a comparison from the system's data, and a measured comparison is a warrant in itself, so the conclusion follows as soon as the data are accepted.
questions.correction: Data do not license conclusions; a principle does. 'Среднее время обработки меньше' supports handing the work over only under a rule such as 'tasks should go where the expected processing time is lowest', and that rule must be stated for a reader to accept or reject it — which is Toulmin's point that an argument is a conclusion based on a fact supported by a warrant, with a possible rebuttal. The reason is also weaker than it looks: no period, no unit and no base are given, and the case mix may differ between the two departments, so an opponent could accept every number and still refuse the conclusion. The repair is not more adjectives; it is one sentence stating the warrant and one sentence naming the figure with its base and period.

questions.prompt: A recommendation table compares two suppliers: «надёжность — 92 процента против 88 процентов», «цена — на 15 процентов ниже», «сроки — 46 дней против 64 дней», and the text concludes «второй вариант надёжнее и дешевле, поэтому выбираем его». What must be fixed before the recommendation can be relied on?
questions.answer: The units and their directions must be made explicit and consistent: '92 процента против 88 процентов' is a rate difference of 4 percentage points, 'на 15 процентов ниже' is a relative change on a stated but unnamed base, and the reliability conclusion contradicts the table, since the higher rate belongs to the first supplier.
questions.distractor: Nothing must be fixed: all four figures have units, and the conclusion simply weighs reliability and price in whatever proportion the writer judges appropriate.
questions.correction: The table mixes a rate expressed in percent, a relative change expressed on an unstated base, and a duration in days, and the conclusion then reverses the reliability comparison — 92 against 88 favours the first supplier, not the second. Even if the reversal is a typo, the recommendation still needs an explicit criterion and an honest hedge, because a weighting that is not stated cannot be argued with and a reader cannot tell which dimension decides the choice. The repairs are to label each rate as a rate and each difference in percentage points, to name the base of the price change, and to write the criterion sentence before the recommendation.

questions.prompt: A presenter reads a written brief aloud to a team. The audience hears: «среднее время обработки снизилось; затраты оцениваются в 180 тысяч рублей; рекомендуется распространить решение». Afterwards someone asks who did what. What conversion was skipped, and what does the presenter need to change?
questions.answer: The presenter skipped the register conversion. Agentless passives and verbal nouns (снизилось, оцениваются, рекомендуется) must become finite active clauses with a stated actor, as Cornell's correspondence between written participles and conversational clauses implies, and the numbers should be rounded aloud with their proportions named rather than read from the page.
questions.distractor: Nothing was skipped: reading the brief aloud is the standard way to present a report, and the audience simply needs to listen more carefully, since Russian formal speech uses the same constructions as formal writing.
questions.correction: Written and spoken Russian distribute the same content differently. Written Russian compresses subordinate material into participles and verbal nouns and suppresses the agent, while speech needs an actor because the audience is watching one and because an unowned claim cannot be judged. The conversion is systematic: снизилось время обработки becomes время обработки упало, оцениваются в becomes стоит около, and рекомендуется распространить becomes мы предлагаем распространить, with the figures rounded honestly and an explicit invitation for questions at the end. A presenter who reads the brief aloud has delivered a form, not a report.

questions.prompt: You are handed two Russian texts about the same fare change. Text A, a news item: «Городская администрация сообщила, что тариф вырастет на пять рублей. По данным департамента транспорта, рост связан с обновлением подвижного состава.» Text B, a notice on a station wall: «Согласно постановлению, проезд подорожает с 1 сентября. Оплата наличными не допускается.» Which text lets you find out who is accountable for the fare change, and which tells you what you must do, and how do the grammatical devices differ?
questions.answer: Text A is the accountable one: it names городская администрация as the source of the claim through сообщила and hands the stated cause to a document through по данным, so both can be asked. Text B is the binding one for behaviour: согласно постановлению names a legal act in the dative, and не допускается states a prohibition impersonally, so it tells a traveller what is forbidden without naming anyone who decided it.
questions.distractor: Both texts are equally accountable, because both name an institution — the administration and the postановление — and an institution is a source in either register.
questions.correction: Naming an institution is not the same as attributing a claim to it. In Text A, the reporting verb сообщила makes the administration the agent of the act of stating, and по данным makes a document the basis of a causal claim, so a reader can request both. In Text B, согласно постановлению is a prepositional government pattern that references a legal act as the authority for a rule, and не допускается suppresses the actor entirely, which is what makes a rule universal and also what makes it impossible to ask the notice a question. The two registers are not competing accounts of the same fact: one is a report about a decision, the other is the decision as it reaches you. Reading them together is the practical skill — and the correct order is to ask Text A who decided and Text B what it obliges.

questions.prompt: A first-person text ends: «Первый месяц мне казалось, что я не понимаю ничего. Потом я начала читать вслух, и через два месяца оказалось, что понимаю почти всё. Зато говорить я до сих пор боюсь. Честно говоря, я путаю падежи.» Compress this into a 25-word Russian summary that keeps the narrator's own arc, then state in English what your compression had to keep and what it was allowed to drop.
questions.answer: A defensible compression: «Сначала ей казалось, что она не понимает ничего; после двух месяцев чтения вслух оказалось, что понимает почти всё, но говорить до сих пор боится». Kept: the initial misapprehension with мне казалось, the revision with оказалось, the concession with зато/но, and the first-person perspective. Dropped: честно говоря and путаю падежи, which are a second concession rather than a step in the arc.
questions.distractor: A defensible compression: «Она читала вслух два месяца и стала лучше понимать; она всё ещё путает падежи». Kept: the outcome and the remaining weakness. Dropped: the opening frame, which is narrative decoration.
questions.correction: Dropping мне казалось and оказалось removes the only signals that the second statement revises the first, and the compressed text then reads as a plain improvement story in which the narrator's fear of speaking appears to contradict her progress. Keeping the revision markers is what preserves the narrator's arc; the honest concession about cases can be dropped because it is another instance of the same point (the speaker's self-assessment), not a new step. Note the dropped item in the wrong answer also loses the tense distinction between a past event and a habit still running, which is exactly the давно-style error of lesson 93.

questions.prompt: A release states: «Доля заявок, обработанных за сутки, выросла с 40 до 52 процентов, рост — 12 процентов. Затраты на внедрение составили около 180 тысяч рублей, что на треть дешевле первоначальной оценки в 240 тысяч.» Recompute both claims, decide which is wrong as written, and say how a careful Russian summary should state each one.
questions.answer: The first claim mixes units: 52 minus 40 equals 12 percentage points, while 52 divided by 40 equals 1.3, so the relative increase is 30 percent, not 12 percent. The second claim checks out: 240 minus 180 equals 60, and 60 divided by 240 equals 0.25, so 180 is 25 percent below 240 — close to, but not exactly, a third, which is why the phrase 'на треть' should be replaced by a figure or by 'примерно на четверть'.
questions.distractor: Both claims are correct as written: 12 percentage points is 12 percent, and 180 is a third less than 240 because the difference is 60 and 60 is a substantial part of 240.
questions.correction: A difference between two rates is measured in percentage points, and a change in a rate relative to its own base is measured in percent — here 30 percent, since 52 divided by 40 is 1.3. For the second claim, the arithmetic gives exactly 25 percent: 60 divided by 240 is 0.25, so 'на треть' overstates the saving by about eight percentage points of the comparison. A careful summary keeps the base with each figure ('с 40 до 52 процентов', 'по сравнению с первоначальной оценкой в 240 тысяч') and either states the computed percentage or replaces the approximation with a hedge that matches the arithmetic.

questions.prompt: A rental advertisement reads: «Уютная квартира рядом с метро. Возможна регистрация. Хозяин не против животных. Цена — от 45 000 рублей.» A reader plans to sign and to keep a cat. Which sentences can the reader rely on, which must be converted into questions, and how should the questions be worded in Russian?
questions.answer: Only the price floor is a statement with a determinate reading — от 45 000 рублей fixes a lower bound, not a rent — and everything else is a hedge or a presupposition to be converted into questions: possible registration is not registration, and 'the owner is not against animals' presupposes that the question arises and says nothing about a deposit or a limit. The questions should ask for the act and the document: «Регистрацию оформляете вы или я?», «Разрешение на животное будет в договоре?», «Полная стоимость аренды — сколько в месяц?»
questions.distractor: The reader can rely on all four sentences, because a Russian advertisement is legally binding on the advertiser and возможна means that registration is available on request.
questions.correction: Возможна is a hedge that marks possibility and commits the writer to nothing, while 'не против' is a presupposition trigger: it takes for granted that animals are an issue and answers a narrower question than the reader is asking. The price figure with от is a floor, exactly the pattern lesson 95 identified in job advertisements. The discipline is to sort each sentence into asserted, presupposed and invited, then rely only on the asserted column and put everything else into questions with an explicit act and object. This is a comprehension exercise in Russian; for a rental contract the questions belong to the reader and, where money or law is involved, to a qualified human reader.

questions.prompt: You must send a Russian text of 120 words in two versions: a written summary of a report for a director who will not read the original, and a spoken explanation of the same report to a team. Name the four things that must appear in both versions, and the three that must differ. Give one example of a sentence that belongs in the written version and one that belongs in the spoken version.
questions.answer: In both: the aim, the figures with their units and bases, the attribution of each claim, and the sentence naming what would change the conclusion. Different: the agency (suppressed in writing, stated in speech), the compression devices (participles and verbal nouns in writing, finite clauses and который-clauses in speech), and the rounding of numbers (exact in writing, honestly rounded with named proportions in speech). Written example: «Среднее время обработки снизилось с 3,2 до 2,1 дня; по данным отдела, доля заявок, закрытых за сутки, выросла с 40 до 52 процентов». Spoken example: «Время обработки упало с трёх дней с небольшим до двух, а больше половины заявок мы теперь закрываем за сутки — раньше это были примерно две из пяти».
questions.distractor: In both: the aim, the figures and the recommendation. Different: the length and the politeness level, since the director is addressed formally and the team informally, while the grammar stays the same in both versions.
questions.correction: Politeness is not the register variable that matters here; agency, compression and rounding are. The written version can leave the actor out because the reader has the document in hand and needs the structure; the spoken version must name the actor because the audience is judging the claim against a person. Rounding in speech is legitimate only if the proportion is named honestly — 'две из пяти' is exactly 40 percent, whereas 'каждая третья' would misstate it. Both versions need the change-of-mind sentence, because without it neither the director nor the team can tell what would make you revise, and the attribution must survive in both, or a summary has become an assertion.

questions.prompt: You disagree with a colleague's proposal in writing. Which arrangement best satisfies both the argument structure and the politeness register, and why? Option A: state the objection first, concede part of it with отчасти, give one measured reason, reply to the strongest counter-argument, and end with a dated review. Option B: state agreement in the opening line, then list three reasons against the proposal, then close with «с уважением».
questions.answer: Option A. It puts the negative claim where a reader can see immediately what is being opposed, concedes a real portion of the objection with отчасти so that the reply addresses the strongest version of the other side, gives a measurable reason with its own support, and ends with a review date that makes the disagreement revisable rather than personal.
questions.distractor: Option B, because agreement and politeness are the same thing in Russian correspondence, and three reasons always outweigh one.
questions.correction: Option B opens with agreement and then contradicts it, which reads as a formula rather than a position, and politeness in Russian official correspondence comes from the register and the fixed formulas, not from assenting to a claim you intend to reject. The number of reasons is not the criterion; the criteria are whether the claim is identifiable, whether the reason has a base, whether the objection is answered as stated, and whether you have said what would change your mind. A dated review is the device that makes all four visible at once, and it costs the writer nothing.

questions.prompt: A written report contains: «По результатам анализа, проведённого отделом в марте, доля отказов, зафиксированных по техническим причинам, снизилась с 12 до 9 процентов, что объясняется заменой оборудования.» Rewrite the same content as a spoken explanation for a team meeting, and state which grammatical items changed and what information you added or dropped in doing so.
questions.answer: Spoken version: «В марте мы провели анализ. Отказы по техническим причинам снизились с двенадцати процентов до девяти — это минус три процентных пункта. Мы думаем, что причина в замене оборудования». Changed: the participial phrase проведённого отделом became a finite clause with мы; the nominalised доля отказов, зафиксированных по техническим причинам became a clause with a finite verb; the passive explanation что объясняется became an active claim of belief (мы думаем), which is more honest than the written version because the written form presented a hypothesis as an explanation.
questions.distractor: Spoken version: «Доля отказов снизилась на три процента, что объясняется заменой оборудования». Changed: nothing except the omission of the date, because speech is written language pronounced aloud.
questions.correction: Two things go wrong in the distractor. First, the register does not change at all, so the audience hears participial and passive constructions read from a page — the failure mode lesson 100 describes. Second, the arithmetic turns a difference of three percentage points into 'на три процента', which is a different claim, since 9 divided by 12 equals 0.75, so the relative fall is 25 percent. The spoken rewrite names the actor, replaces the passive explanation with an attributed belief, and keeps the unit correct, which is what makes speech both clearer and more honest than the written original it came from.

questions.prompt: A rule sheet says: «Сотрудникам необходимо сдавать пропуска при выходе. Не надо оставлять личные вещи в переговорных. Посетители без пропуска не допускаются.» You must explain these rules to a new colleague in speech. Which of the three sentences needs repair in your explanation, and what is the risk of each reading?
questions.answer: The second sentence needs repair: не надо is ambiguous between 'must not' and 'need not', with the usual reading being prohibition, so an explanation should state the intended rule explicitly rather than repeat it — «Личные вещи в переговорных не оставляйте», or if the rule is optional, «Вещи можно не оставлять». The other two are unambiguous: сдавать must be read as an impersonal necessity with a dative doer (сотрудникам), and не допускаются as an impersonal prohibition on visitors.
questions.distractor: The first sentence needs repair, because необходимо with a dative is a weaker obligation than должен and can be ignored; the other two are clear.
questions.correction: Необходимо is not weaker than должен; it is the impersonal form of the same strength, and the difference is grammatical rather than modal — with необходимо the doer is in the dative and the sentence has no subject, while with должен the doer is nominative. The ambiguity lies in не надо, which Cornell's grammar describes as able to mean either mustn't or don't have to, with the prohibition reading as the default, and for which the unambiguous no-necessity form is a form of мочь with не before an imperfective infinitive. In an oral explanation you have one more resource than the sheet: you can name the rule and its consequence, which is what a new colleague actually needs.

questions.prompt: Compare what lessons 90 and 100 ask of you: a sustained conversation about work, study and plans, and a written brief plus a spoken presentation. Name two skills the presentation demands that the conversation did not, and two that the conversation demanded and the presentation does not.
questions.answer: Presentation-only: re-deriving the same content in two registers, and carrying units and bases unchanged from a written table into speech under questioning. Conversation-only: managing turn-taking and repair in real time, and negotiating meaning with an interlocutor who interrupts and disagrees unpredictably.
questions.distractor: Presentation-only: politeness formulas and formal address. Conversation-only: the past tense and everyday vocabulary.
questions.correction: Politeness and basic tenses run through both, so they cannot distinguish the two tasks. The real asymmetry is structural. A presentation is prepared and can be revised; it therefore demands the register conversion and the discipline of stating units, bases and the change-of-mind condition, because the question period will test exactly those. A conversation cannot be revised and it is jointly produced; it therefore demands real-time repair (Повторите, пожалуйста; я не совсем понимаю), reading of turn-taking signals, and the ability to concede a point quickly without losing the thread. A learner who has written and rehearsed a brief has not thereby practised interruption, and a learner who can hold a conversation has not thereby learned to present figures that survive an audience's arithmetic.

questions.prompt: A Russian article says: «По словам представителя компании, выручка выросла примерно вдвое; в отчёте указано, что рост составил 96 процентов, а число заказов почти не изменилось.» A reader concludes that the company's revenue doubled because more orders were placed. Where has the reader misread the language, and what would a correct reading say?
questions.answer: The reader has misread three items at once: 'по словам представителя' is attributed speech rather than an assertion of the article's author, 'примерно вдвое' is a rough spoken-style approximation for a figure the report states precisely as 96 percent, and 'число заказов почти не изменилось' rules out the explanation the reader supplied, since revenue can rise without more orders if the average order value or the price changed.
questions.distractor: The reader has misread only the arithmetic: 96 percent and двое are not the same thing, so the figure must be wrong rather than the interpretation.
questions.correction: The arithmetic is nearly consistent — 'примерно вдвое' and 96 percent are compatible, since 96 percent is a little less than doubling — and the error is not there. The errors are attribution, approximation and causal inference. По словам plus a genitive source hands the claim to a person who may be speaking in his own interest; примерно is a hedge that the report's precise figure replaces rather than confirms; and почти не изменилось names a quantity that did not move, which makes the reader's explanation of the rise impossible to derive from the text as given. A correct reading states what is attributed and to whom, what the precise figure is, and what remains unexplained — in this case, whether the change came from prices or from the composition of orders, which the text does not say.

questions.prompt: A regulation contains: «Осуществление контроля за соблюдением сроков передачи документов возлагается на руководителя подразделения.» Identify the actor, the action and the object, state what the sentence does not tell you, and say why the register is built this way.
questions.answer: Actor: руководитель подразделения, named in the accusative after возлагается на. Action: осуществление контроля, a verbal noun meaning 'the carrying out of control'. Object: the deadlines for transferring documents, inside the phrase за соблюдением сроков передачи документов. The sentence does not say what counts as a breach, who else may check, or what happens if the deadlines are missed, and the register suppresses the individual by making the action a noun and the obligation a property of the office rather than of a person.
questions.distractor: Actor: не specified, because the sentence has no nominative subject and therefore no responsible person; the regulation is a statement of policy rather than an assignment of duty.
questions.correction: The absence of a nominative subject does not mean the absence of an actor: возлагается на plus the accusative names the person the duty falls to, which is the same construction that lets a rule sheet bind someone without naming them as a grammatical subject. The verbal noun осуществление is what makes the sentence hard: it converts a verb into a noun so that the duty can be assigned to an office, and it is the register feature lesson 92 documented as compression and standard arrangement. The practical reading is to convert the nominalised sentence back into a plain one before deciding what you are obliged to do: руководитель подразделения контролирует, соблюдаются ли сроки передачи документов. Anything the plain version cannot state is a question for the institution, not an inference you should make.

questions.prompt: You must write a 60-word Russian abstract of a report whose findings are: an attributed and hedged result (по данным отдела, среднее время обработки снизилось примерно на треть), a rate comparison (доля заявок, закрытых за сутки, выросла с 40 до 52 процентов), and a stated limitation (данные охватывают только один регион). Write the abstract, then list the four checks a reader of your abstract should be able to perform on it.
questions.answer: Model abstract: «Пилот проводился в одном регионе. По данным отдела, среднее время обработки заявки снизилось примерно на треть. Доля заявок, закрытых за сутки, выросла с 40 до 52 процентов, то есть на 12 процентных пунктов. Данные охватывают только один регион, поэтому выводы предварительны.» The four checks: (1) is each claim attributed to its source; (2) does each figure carry its unit and base, with the rate difference stated in percentage points; (3) has the hedge approximately на треть survived as a hedge rather than become a precise figure; (4) has the limitation been kept in the text rather than moved to a footnote.
questions.distractor: Model abstract: «Время обработки снизилось на 33 процента, доля заявок за сутки выросла на 12 процентов, что доказывает эффективность пилота.» The checks are the same four, and this version passes them because the figures are computed rather than hedged.
questions.correction: The distractor fails three of the four checks and invents a fifth problem: 33 процента converts a hedge into a measurement (примерно на треть is not 33 percent, and the base of the reduction is not stated), 12 percent mislabels a difference of 12 percentage points, and доказательство эффективности is a conclusion the data do not license — the pilot covered one region and the abstract should say so rather than argue. The checks are the summary discipline of lesson 96 combined with the unit discipline of lesson 94: attribution, unit and base, preserved hedge, preserved limitation. An abstract that passes all four is shorter than the report and no stronger than it, which is the definition of an honest compression.
